title: Spicy Shrimp, Vegetable & Couscous Bowls
ingredients: ½ cup snow peas, trimmed and sliced
1 large garlic clove, crushed and peeled
1 lb raw shrimp (16–20 count), peeled and deveined
steps: Cook couscous as directed on package; drain and rinse. Combine with bell pepper, snow peas, 2 tbsp each basil and mint.
Blend cilantro, lime juice, vinegar, water, sambal, ginger, garlic, ¼ tsp pepper and salt. With blender running, drizzle in 4 tbsp oil. Reserve 2 tbsp dressing; toss remainder with couscous mixture.

Heat remaining 1 tbsp oil over high heat. Dry shrimp, season with remaining ¼ tsp pepper, and cook about 2 minutes per side until just done. Serve over couscous, drizzled with reserved dressing and remaining herbs.

title: Creamy Harissa Chicken Cutlets
steps: Season chicken with ⅛ tsp each salt and pepper. Heat oil in skillet over medium-high; cook chicken, turning once, until browned and center reaches 165°F, about 6 minutes. Set aside.
Stir harissa and garlic in skillet for 1 minute. Add wine and scrape pan; simmer about 2 minutes until mostly evaporated.
Reduce heat to medium. Add cream, chicken juices and remaining ⅛ tsp each salt and pepper; simmer 2 minutes. Stir in kale, return chicken and coat in sauce.

title: Roast Pork Loin with Salsa Verde
ingredients: ½ cup extra-virgin olive oil plus 2 tbsp, divided
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Season pork with ¾ tsp salt. Place fat-side down in large roasting pan or cast-iron skillet; cook over low heat 15–20 minutes until fat is browned and crisp.
Turn pork over with tongs; roast until internal temperature reaches 145°F, 35–45 minutes. Rest on cutting board for 10 minutes.

Blend chervil, cilantro, parsley, ½ cup oil, ice cube, lemon zest, juice and garlic until smooth. Stir in remaining 2 tbsp oil and ½ tsp salt. Slice pork thinly and serve with drippings and salsa verde.

title: Orange & Fennel Sausage Patties
ingredients: 1 small leek, white and light green part only, finely chopped and rinsed
steps: Heat 2 tsp oil over medium-high. Cook leek until tender and beginning to brown, about 2 minutes; add garlic for 30 seconds. Mix in orange zest and cool about 5 minutes.
Combine pork, wine, vinegar, salt and spices in a bowl. Mix in leek mixture without overworking. Divide into 8 balls; flatten to ½-inch patties.
Heat remaining 2 tsp oil over medium-high. Cook patties in two batches, about 2–3 minutes per side, until browned and internal temperature is 165°F.

title: Lemon Chicken Orzo Soup with Kale
ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts, trimmed and cut into 1-inch pieces
1 tsp dried oregano and/or thyme, divided
⅔ cup orzo pasta, preferably whole wheat
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in large pot over medium-high. Season chicken with ½ tsp oregano/thyme, ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper. Cook until lightly browned, 3–5 minutes, then transfer to a plate.
Add remaining oil, onions, carrots and celery; cook 3–5 minutes until softened. Add garlic, bay leaf and remaining ½ tsp herbs; stir 30–60 seconds.
Add broth, bring to a boil, then add orzo. Simmer covered 5 minutes. Add kale, chicken and any juices; cook another 5–8 minutes until pasta is tender and chicken cooked through.
Remove bay leaf. Stir in lemon zest and juice, remaining ¾ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper.

title: Fish Chowder with Fennel & Corn
ingredients: 1 small fennel bulb, cored and diced (reserve fronds)
1 celery stalk, diced (reserve tender green leaves)
1 lb russet potatoes, peeled and diced
2 lb skinned fish, cut into 1-inch pieces
Dash of Tabasco, or to taste
steps: Cook bacon in large pot over medium heat until fat renders, about 5 minutes; remove bacon. Add onion, fennel, shallot, celery, corn, thyme and white pepper; cook 3–5 minutes until softened.
Stir in flour 1–2 minutes, then add stock and simmer. Add potatoes; cook 18–22 minutes until tender and broth thickens.

Add cream and return to simmer. Add fish, partially cover and cook about 5 minutes until just done. Stir in Tabasco, Worcestershire, salt and pepper. Garnish with reserved bacon, fennel fronds, celery leaves and piment d’Espelette.

title: Goat Cheese Crostini with Mushrooms & Brown Butter
steps: Heat oil in medium skillet over medium heat. Crisp sage leaves 2–4 seconds per side; transfer to paper towel.
Cook mushrooms and shallot in same pan with salt and pepper, stirring occasionally, about 5 minutes until lightly browned. Transfer mushrooms to a bowl.
Brown butter in pan, scraping browned bits, about 30 seconds. Pour over mushrooms and mix.
Spread goat cheese over toast; top with mushrooms, pine nuts and sage.

title: Blackened Honey-Glazed Salmon Bites
ingredients: 1½ lb skinless salmon fillet, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 (1-inch) piece ginger, peeled and finely chopped
steps: Whisk soy sauce, Cajun seasoning, and 2 tbsp honey. Add salmon, coat gently, and marinate 10 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Brown half the salmon, turning occasionally, 4–5 minutes. Transfer to a plate; repeat with remaining salmon. Reserve marinade; wipe skillet.
Whisk 4 tbsp lime juice into reserved marinade with remaining 6 tbsp honey.

Heat remaining 1 tbsp oil in skillet over medium heat. Stir in garlic and ginger about 1 minute. Add marinade and cook until thickened, 3–4 minutes. Return salmon to skillet and toss gently in glaze; remove from heat.
Toss cucumbers, avocado, shallot, red pepper flakes, 2 tbsp cilantro, and remaining 2 tbsp lime juice; season with salt.
Serve salmon topped with remaining cilantro, with rice and cucumber salad.

title: Minty Meatballs with Lemon Orzo
ingredients: 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
3 tbsp finely chopped fresh mint, plus whole leaves for serving
1 tsp finely grated lemon zest, plus more for serving
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Line baking sheet with parchment and drizzle with oil. Mix egg, turkey, panko, chopped mint, paprika, one-third of garlic, and 1 tbsp oil; season. Form 18 meatballs (about 1½-inch) and place on sheet.
Bake meatballs, shaking sheet halfway through, until cooked through and golden, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile melt butter in large straight-sided skillet over medium-high heat. Cook remaining garlic about 1 minute; add orzo and toast about 2 minutes.
Add broth, season, bring to boil, then simmer over medium-low, stirring frequently, 10–12 minutes until orzo is tender and liquid mostly absorbed.
Stir in spinach, lemon zest, lemon juice, and ½ cup feta until spinach wilts, about 2 minutes; season.
Divide orzo into bowls, top with meatballs, remaining feta, mint leaves, lemon zest, and a drizzle of oil.

title: Shawarma-Stuffed Peppers
ingredients: ¼ cup fresh mint leaves, chopped, plus more for serving
¼ cup fresh parsley leaves, chopped, plus more for serving
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Halve and seed peppers, place cut-side up in 13-by-9-inch baking dish, drizzle with 1 tsp oil, season, then turn cut-side down.
Roast peppers until just tender, about 12 minutes; turn cut-side up.
Beat egg in large bowl; add turkey, scallions, couscous, mint, parsley, coriander, cumin, turmeric, cinnamon, cayenne, 1 tsp garlic, and 1 tbsp water. Mix by hand.
Divide filling among peppers. Drizzle with 1 tbsp water and remaining 1 tsp oil; cover with foil.
Roast about 35 minutes until filling is cooked through. Uncover, baste with juices, and roast 5 minutes more to lightly brown.
Combine mayonnaise, sour cream, lemon juice, 2 tbsp water, and remaining 1 tsp garlic; season.
Top peppers with tomatoes, mint, parsley, and mayo sauce.

title: Shepherd’s Pie Potato Skins
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Poke potatoes with fork. Drizzle with 1 tbsp oil and microwave on high 7 minutes; flip and microwave about 7 minutes more until tender.
Heat remaining 1 tbsp oil in skillet over medium-high. Brown beef 5–6 minutes, season, transfer to plate; pour off drippings except 1 tbsp.

Cook onion and carrot about 5 minutes; add garlic, rosemary, and thyme for 1 minute. Return beef. Cook tomato paste until brick red, 2–3 minutes; add wine and reduce 2–3 minutes. Add broth and Worcestershire; simmer. Stir in flour and cook until thickened, about 2 minutes. Add corn and peas.
Cut one rounded long side from each potato; scoop out flesh leaving ¼-inch shell. Place flesh in bowl.
Melt butter and stir into potato flesh with half-and-half, 2 tbsp Parmesan, and 1 tbsp parsley; season.
Set shells in baking dish, fill with beef mixture, top with mashed potato and remaining Parmesan.
Bake 30–35 minutes until browning. Broil about 5 minutes, watching closely; top with remaining parsley.

title: Beef Noodle Casserole
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Cook noodles in salted boiling water 1 minute shy of al dente; drain, reserving 1 cup pasta water. Toss noodles with butter.
In another pot over medium-high heat, heat oil. Brown beef about 6 minutes, season.

Reduce heat to medium. Cook onion and garlic until translucent, 4–5 minutes. Add tomato sauce, soup, cream, and one-third of cheddar. Simmer; add ½–1 cup pasta water as needed until cheese melts and sauce reaches desired consistency. Season. Stir in noodles.
Transfer to 13-by-9-inch baking pan and top with remaining cheddar. Bake about 30 minutes until bubbling; garnish with parsley.

ingredients: ⅓ cup finely chopped flat-leaf parsley
2 tbsp plus 1 tsp finely chopped chives
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp good-quality white wine vinegar
⅛ tsp freshly ground black pepper
steps: Combine olive oil with parsley, chives, and tarragon in a small bowl immediately after chopping to preserve their color.
In another small bowl, combine shallot, vinegar, and half the salt; add more vinegar if necessary to cover shallot. Allow to macerate.
No more than 15 minutes before serving, combine herb oil and shallot mixture. Season with remaining salt, pepper, sugar, and additional vinegar or oil to taste. Serve immediately.

title: Spring Pea–Mint Relish
steps: Warm olive oil in saucepan over medium heat to about 150°F, warm but not hot. Add peas, reduce heat to low, and cook gently 3–4 minutes until barely cooked and bright green. Lift peas out and reserve oil.
Warm 2 tbsp reserved oil over medium-low. Add garlic and chile flakes; sweat about 1 minute until lightly cooked.

Pulse cooked peas, garlic-chile oil, mint, lemon zest, and ¼ cup reserved pea oil in a food processor 3–4 times to make a coarse relish, not a smooth purée. Add a little more oil if needed; season with salt. Serve immediately.

title: Savory Tomato Confiture
ingredients: ½ cup finely minced yellow onion
½ tsp toasted and ground cumin seeds
½ tsp toasted and ground coriander seeds
¼ tsp fennel pollen or toasted and ground fennel seeds
½ tsp freshly ground black pepper
¼ cup packed light or dark brown sugar
steps: Heat oil in a 4-quart nonreactive saucepan over medium heat. Sweat onion, shallot, and garlic 2–3 minutes. Add cumin, coriander, chile, orange zest, fennel, salt, pepper, and mustard seeds; cook about 1 minute.
Add tomato paste and stir until oil begins separating, about 30 seconds. Add sugar, stirring until melted and bubbling, about 1 minute. Add vinegar and let bubble about 30 seconds.

Add tomatoes; reduce heat to low and cook, stirring often, 25–30 minutes until deeply flavored. Adjust vinegar or spice to taste. Refrigerate in airtight container up to 10 days; bring to room temperature before serving.

title: Tomatoes with Crab, Sungold Tomato French Dressing & Fried Caper Rémoulade
ingredients: ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
⅛ tsp freshly ground black pepper
⅓ cup Fried Caper Rémoulade (see R019)
4 oz fresh-cooked crabmeat, picked over for shell fragments
Freshly ground black pepper, for finishing
steps: For dressing, heat 2 tbsp olive oil in small saucepan over medium-high. Add Sungold tomatoes and cook until they begin to burst, about 1 minute.
Add garlic, ½ tsp salt, and pepper; cook until garlic is soft and translucent, about 1 minute. Add honey and cook until large bubbles form, 15–20 seconds. Add vinegar; remove from heat.
Blend tomato mixture on high 20–30 seconds; strain into bowl. Whisk in remaining 2 tbsp oil and remaining ¼ tsp salt; adjust seasoning.
Slice heirloom tomatoes about ¼ inch thick and season with salt and pepper. Put 1 tbsp dressing in center of each of four plates; arrange tomato slices over dressing.
Spoon about 1½ tbsp rémoulade in center of tomatoes. Divide crab among plates. Garnish with chive batons, edible flowers if using, and black pepper; serve immediately.

title: Pan-Seared Wild Mushrooms with Parsley and Parmesan
ingredients: 2 lb wild mushrooms (such as chanterelle or porcini), cleaned
4 garlic cloves, smashed with flat side of knife
½ cup roughly chopped flat-leaf parsley
steps: Quarter large mushrooms and halve medium ones, leaving small mushrooms whole. Divide into four batches.

Heat black steel pan over high heat until very hot. Add 1 tbsp oil and one batch mushrooms, ½–¾ tsp salt, and ¼ tsp pepper. Lower heat to medium-high; add one garlic clove and sauté 7–8 minutes until browning and moisture evaporates.

Add thyme sprig during final minute, then 1 tbsp butter and cook 1–2 minutes more. Transfer mushrooms to bowl; discard garlic and thyme. Repeat for remaining three batches with remaining oil, mushrooms, seasonings, garlic, thyme, and butter.
Return all mushrooms to stainless-steel pan over medium heat to warm. Drizzle with sherry vinegar, sprinkle parsley, toss with Parmesan shavings until just softened, and serve.

title: Buttermilk–Black Pepper Ice Cream
ingredients: 1¼ cups sugar, divided (1 cup + ¼ cup)
1 teaspoon toasted and very coarsely ground black peppercorns, divided
steps: Set a fine-mesh strainer over a bowl. In a small heavy saucepan, heat cream and 1 cup sugar over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves, until steaming and small bubbles form at the edges (about 190°F), 4–5 minutes.
While cream heats, whisk egg yolks, remaining ¼ cup sugar, and salt in a bowl until yolks lighten, about 2 minutes.

Remove hot cream from heat. Gradually whisk hot cream into yolks, one ladle at a time. Return mixture to saucepan and cook over low heat, stirring slowly with a spatula, until thick enough to coat the spatula (about 170°F). Do not scramble the eggs.

Immediately pour custard through strainer to remove any bits of cooked egg. Stir in ¾ teaspoon ground black pepper. Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours or up to 24 hours until completely cold (or chill in an ice bath).
Add vanilla and buttermilk to cold custard and whisk well. Taste and add remaining ¼ teaspoon pepper if desired.
Churn in an ice cream maker following manufacturer instructions. Transfer to container and freeze until hardened, about 2 hours. If too firm to scoop, let stand at room temperature 10–15 minutes.

title: Fried Caper Rémoulade
ingredients: 1 cup homemade aioli (see Aioli and Variations, R020)
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp finely minced cornichon
⅛ tsp freshly ground black pepper
¼ cup capers, brined or salt-packed
1½ cups canola oil, for frying (most is not absorbed)
steps: Combine aioli, cornichon, lemon zest, lemon juice, chives, celery, sugar, and black pepper; mix well.

Prepare capers: for brined capers, drain and press gently between paper or cloth towels until completely dry. For salt-packed capers, soak in warm water for about 10 minutes, then fresh water for 5 minutes; drain and dry thoroughly.
Heat canola oil in a 2-quart saucepan to 350°F. Fry capers about 2 minutes until they open like flowers and become crunchy.
Remove capers with a slotted spoon to paper towel and cool completely, about 5 minutes. Stir into aioli mixture just before serving so they stay crisp.

title: Aioli and Variations
ingredients: 1 egg (use yolk; briefly coddled in shell as directed)
½ cup neutral oil, such as canola or grapeseed
1½ tsp lemon juice mixed with 2 tsp room-temperature water
½ tsp garlic paste (see source cookbook page 344)
steps: Submerge the whole egg, still in its shell, in boiling water for 1 minute. Remove, crack, separate the yolk into a small bowl, and discard the white. Note: this brief coddling is not a reliable pasteurization step.
Combine the olive oil and neutral oil in a squeeze bottle or flexible container for controlled pouring. Whisk the yolk until broken up and smooth.
While whisking constantly, add the oils very slowly, initially just a drop or two at a time. Continue adding the oils in a very fine stream, whisking steadily to maintain an emulsion.
When the yolk mixture begins to look slightly stringy or taffy-like (often after about 2 minutes of whisking), whisk in about ½ tsp of the diluted lemon juice to thin it. Resume adding oil slowly.
If the mixture becomes tight again, add another scant ½ tsp of diluted lemon juice. Continue until all oil and diluted lemon juice are incorporated. Whisk in garlic paste and salt to taste.
Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container; the cookbook recommends using within 2 days. For lower food-safety risk, use pasteurized eggs, especially for vulnerable diners.

title: Crispy, Crunchy Brocc & Grains
ingredients: 2 oz smoked cheddar or other hard smoked cheese
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
½ cup grains such as farro, wheatberries, or barley
Extra-virgin olive oil (for roasting, dressing, and crisping)
3 tbsp white wine vinegar or champagne vinegar
steps: Heat oven to 450°F with two racks in lower third. Cook ½ cup grains in salted boiling water until tender but not mushy, about 10 minutes for farro (other grains vary). Drain and cool.

Cut broccoli into 2-inch pieces, separating florets and stems; discard only woody ends. Divide between two rimmed sheets, coat generously with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast 18–24 minutes, switching sheets halfway, until deeply charred underneath.
Finely chop chile (discard seeds) and thinly slice shallot. Whisk with 3 tbsp vinegar, a couple tablespoons olive oil, and a pinch of salt in a large bowl.
Heat about 2 tbsp olive oil in nonstick skillet over medium. Crisp cooled grains undisturbed 2–3 minutes, then stir and cook another 1–2 minutes until golden; salt and transfer to dressing.
Crumble 2 oz smoked cheese, add to bowl with leaves from herb bunch. Add roasted broccoli, toss, season and serve.

title: Monochromatic Melon Salad
ingredients: 2 medium fennel bulbs (about 1 lb), with fronds if available
½ small ripe honeydew or cantaloupe (¾ lb)
5 oz Parmigiano Reggiano, in wedge form
Flaky sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
steps: Chop about ¼ cup fennel fronds if available. Process with ⅓ cup pistachios and ⅓ cup olive oil until a loose pesto-like oil forms; season with flaky salt.
Remove tough outer layers of fennel, trim root ends, and shave thinly. Cut melon into 2-inch wedges, remove rind, then thinly slice to yield about 10 oz.
Combine fennel and melon. Season with flaky salt and squeeze in juice of 2 lemons (adjust to taste). Gently toss.
Shave 5 oz Parmesan into large shards, add with remaining fronds, and gently toss.
Pile salad into tall tower, drizzling pistachio oil between layers. Finish with flaky salt and black pepper.

title: Cucumber Bag Salad with Miso-Poppy Dressing
steps: Halve cucumbers lengthwise, put in resealable bag with several pinches of salt, press out air and seal. Smash with rolling pin or heavy skillet into irregular bite-size pieces.
Spread cucumbers evenly on a double layer of paper towels on rimmed baking sheet; let drain while making dressing.
Whisk buttermilk, olive oil, white miso, rice vinegar, zest and juice of ½ orange, and poppy seeds in a large bowl until smooth.
Pat cucumbers very dry. Add to dressing with cilantro leaves and tender stems; toss, taste, and season with salt. Serve immediately, or return to bag and refrigerate for transport.

title: Broken Noodle Bolognese
ingredients: 3 tbsp mascarpone cheese, plus more for serving
2 oz grated Parmigiano Reggiano (about ½ cup), plus more for serving
1 lb 80% lean ground beef and/or veal
1 lb spicy Italian sausage, casings removed
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
steps: Finely chop celery, onion, fennel, and rosemary leaves. Mix beef and sausage and divide into four large shaggy balls; season with salt and pepper.
Heat several glugs olive oil in Dutch oven over medium-high until shimmering. Brown meatballs without disturbing, turning to form crust all over, 10–12 minutes. Remove to plate.
Cook celery, onion, fennel, and rosemary in pot, stirring, until softened and starting to stick, 10–13 minutes.
Stir in miso and tomato paste; cook until sizzling and sticking, 3–4 minutes. Add red and white wine and scrape pot. Reduce heat to medium.
Crumble meat into pot; cook, mashing and stirring, until most liquid evaporates, 9–11 minutes. Stir in 2½ cups water, simmer covered on very low 20 minutes to 1½ hours, stirring periodically.
Stir in a couple big spoonfuls mascarpone; simmer uncovered very gently until thick and deeply flavored, 1 hour or longer. Add water if drying out. Keep warm.
Boil salted water. Break lasagna noodles into irregular 2-inch shapes and cook until al dente, about 10 minutes. Reserve a generous cup pasta water.
Warm ragù, add cooked noodles, another spoonful mascarpone and a handful of Parmesan; toss, adding reserved pasta water as needed until saucy. Serve with extra mascarpone, olive oil and Parmesan.

ingredients: 2 oz grated Parmigiano Reggiano (about ½ cup), plus more for serving
1 lb sweet Italian sausage, casings removed
6 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
steps: Boil heavily salted water. Thinly slice shallots; strip collard leaves from stems and cut into 1-inch strips.
Cook orecchiette until al dente. Reserve a few cups pasta water, drain, and drizzle with olive oil to prevent clumping.
Heat several tbsp olive oil in Dutch oven over medium-high. Brown sausage in large pieces 3–4 minutes undisturbed; flip and cook 1–2 minutes. Remove to plate.
Reduce heat to medium-low, add shallots and salt; cook until jammy, about 4 minutes. Stir in tomato paste and 4 tbsp chopped Calabrian chiles (less for milder heat); cook 4–5 minutes until sticking.
Add collards and several splashes pasta water; stir, cover and cook 4–5 minutes until tender. Add more water as needed; keep covered and warm.

Squeeze lemon over pasta. Divide among bowls, add torn burrata if using, drizzle with olive oil, and sprinkle with Parmesan.

title: Skirt Steak with Juicy Tomatoes & Salsa Macha
ingredients: 1½ lb quick-cooking steak, such as skirt or flank
⅓ cup plus 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for pan
1½ tsp chipotle chile powder or smoked paprika
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
4 tbsp apple cider vinegar, plus more to taste
steps: Crush ½ cup roasted peanuts. In a small saucepan combine peanuts, ⅓ cup olive oil and 3 tbsp sesame seeds. Cook over medium-low heat, swirling often, until peanuts are deeply golden and toasted, 4–6 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in red pepper flakes, chipotle powder and 2 tsp kosher salt. Finely grate 3 garlic cloves into the hot salsa macha; stir and set aside.
Cut tomatoes into irregular 1–2-inch shapes. Toss in a bowl with a splash of apple cider vinegar and some kosher salt.

Cut steak crosswise into 5-inch pieces; season all over with kosher salt and black pepper. Coat with a little olive oil. Heat a large cast-iron skillet over high until ripping hot. Add oil, then cook steaks in batches undisturbed until well browned, 2–3 minutes. Flip and cook another 30 seconds to 1 minute for thinner steaks, longer if needed. Transfer to board.
Off heat, add salsa macha to the skillet and scrape up browned bits. Stir in a few more tablespoons of apple cider vinegar to taste.
Slice steaks crosswise and arrange on a platter. Spoon tomatoes and their juices over steak, drizzle with warm salsa macha, and finish with flaky sea salt.

title: Molle Balls

½ lb spicy Italian sausage, casings removed
4 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling and browning
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
6 oil-packed anchovy fillets, plus 1½ tsp of their oil
steps: Whisk 2 large eggs with 6 grated garlic cloves, ricotta, 2 oz Parmesan, 2 tbsp olive oil, 2½ tsp salt, 1½ tsp anchovy oil and lots of black pepper. Whisk in 1¼ cups panko until hydrated.
Finely chop leaves from about half the mint bunch. Add mint and ½ lb sausage, working it in by hand. Add ¾ lb ground beef and gently combine. Divide into 8 tennis-ball-sized meatballs.

Finely slice the onion and remaining 6 garlic cloves. In a large Dutch oven, heat a few glugs olive oil over high. Brown meatballs in a single layer, turning every minute or so, 6–7 minutes total. Transfer to a plate; they will finish cooking in sauce. Pour off all but 2 tbsp fat.
Reduce heat to medium; add onion, sliced garlic, 6 oil-packed anchovies and a pinch of red pepper flakes. Stir until onion is translucent and beginning to brown, 6–8 minutes.

Stir in 28 oz tomato purée, 3 tbsp butter and a few mint sprigs, reserving mint for garnish. Season generously with salt; bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to maintain a gentle simmer and cook until slightly thickened, 4–6 minutes.

Nestle meatballs into sauce, cover and cook over medium heat, turning occasionally, 8 minutes. Uncover and continue cooking until meatballs are springy, cooked through and sauce is reduced, 8–10 minutes. Ensure ground meat reaches 160°F.
Scatter remaining mint leaves over meatballs; grate Parmesan over top and drizzle with olive oil. Serve with garlic-rubbed toast if desired.

title: Crispy Salmon with Coconut Rice & Crackle Sauce
steps: Rinse 2 cups long-grain white rice in a fine-mesh strainer until water runs clear. Drain and transfer to a medium saucepan with a tight-fitting lid.

Open coconut milk; reserve a few tablespoons in a small bowl. Add remaining coconut milk, rice, ¾ cup water and a big pinch of salt to saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium-high, then reduce heat to very low, cover and cook 16 minutes. Remove from heat and keep covered until serving.
Thinly slice English cucumber, preferably with a mandoline. Toss with salt and chill.

Chop or coarsely crush ½ cup peanuts. In a large nonstick skillet combine peanuts, ¼ cup olive oil and 3 tbsp sesame seeds. Cook over medium heat, stirring often, until peanuts are several shades darker and sesame seeds toasted, 6–8 minutes.
Transfer peanut mixture to a small bowl. While hot, stir in 2 grated garlic cloves, grated ginger, 1½ tsp red pepper flakes, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp honey, reserved coconut milk and salt to taste.

Wipe skillet clean. Season salmon with salt. Arrange fillets skin-side down in skillet and set over medium heat. Cook, occasionally pressing gently, until skin is golden and very crisp, 7–9 minutes. Flip and cook until salmon is mostly opaque on sides with a slight translucence, 1–2 minutes more, or to preferred doneness.
Fluff coconut rice, divide among bowls, and top each with salmon, salted cucumber and crackle sauce.

title: Last-Meal Scallops
ingredients: 10 tbsp unsalted butter, at room temperature
1½ lb dry-packed sea scallops (size U10 or U15)
steps: Soften 10 tbsp unsalted butter without melting. Pick parsley leaves and finely chop by hand or in food processor; transfer to a bowl.
Finely grate 8 garlic cloves and zest of 1 lemon into parsley. Add softened butter and a big pinch of salt; mix or pulse until incorporated, scraping sides as needed.
Position rack in top of oven and preheat broiler. Pat scallops very dry and season with salt.
Heat large cast-iron skillet over high. Add enough olive oil to coat surface. When smoking, add scallops in a single layer and cook undisturbed until deep golden crust forms, about 3 minutes.

Transfer scallops momentarily to plate, seared-side up. Discard oil from skillet. Spread generous dollop of garlic-parsley butter (about ½ tbsp) on top of each scallop; return to skillet butter-side up.
Place skillet under broiler until butter melts and scallops have firmed but remain slightly bouncy, 1–2 minutes. Squeeze lemon juice over scallops and serve with crusty bread.

notes: Use dry-packed scallops rather than wet-packed. Broiling and searing are fast; avoid overcooking. Time is estimated.

title: Chicken Piccata with Sweet Corn, Chiles & Buttermilk
ingredients: 1 red Fresno chile, or ¾ tsp red pepper flakes
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
steps: Thinly slice shallots, garlic and Fresno chile. Shuck corn and cut kernels from 2 ears.
Pound chicken thighs between parchment to about ½-inch thickness. Season with salt and pepper. Put ¼ cup flour in shallow bowl and dredge thighs, shaking off excess.

Heat cast-iron skillet over high with about 2 tbsp olive oil. Working in batches, brown thighs deeply on bottom, 4–5 minutes; flip and cook 2 minutes longer. Transfer to plate and repeat with remaining chicken.

Reduce heat to low. Add 2 tbsp butter, anchovies, shallots, garlic, chile and 6 mint sprigs. Season with salt and pepper and sauté, stirring, until aromatics soften, about 3 minutes. Add corn and cook 2 minutes.
Add 1½ cups buttermilk and adjust heat to maintain brisk simmer. Cook, shaking pan and stirring occasionally, until slightly reduced but still saucy, 3–4 minutes; buttermilk may split into curds.
Cube remaining 4 tbsp butter and add to pan, vigorously shaking as it incorporates, about 2 minutes, to form a thick emulsion.
Cut lemons in half. Divide chicken among plates, top with pan sauce, fresh mint and lemon halves for squeezing.

nutrition.source: Not provided in photographed recipe; not estimated

notes: Cookbook uses chicken thighs rather than classic breast cutlets. Verify chicken reaches 165°F before serving. Total time estimated.

title: Chile-Basted Half Chicken with Caper Chimichurri
ingredients: 1 tbsp Aleppo pepper or ¾ tsp red pepper flakes
½ chicken (leg and breast attached), or about 2 lb bone-in skin-on chicken pieces
steps: Preheat oven to 450°F. Slice potato into ¼-inch rounds. Mix 2 finely grated garlic cloves, Aleppo pepper, smoked paprika, and enough olive oil to make a wet-sand-like paste. Pat chicken dry and season with salt.

Heat a little olive oil in a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high until wisps of smoke appear. Brown chicken skin-side down, pressing with a second heavy skillet for even contact, 8–10 minutes. Remove chicken skin-side up.

Layer potato slices in overlapping circles in the skillet. Brush with some chile-garlic oil and season with salt. Set chicken skin-side up on potatoes and brush generously with remaining chile-garlic oil. Roast, basting with pan juices once or twice, until thickest breast meat registers 150°F, about 30 minutes. Transfer chicken to cutting board to rest; return potatoes to oven if needed to crisp.

Chop shallot, cilantro, and serrano. Pulse in food processor with remaining garlic clove and capers; add ¼ cup olive oil and sherry vinegar, then blend until combined but not completely smooth. Season with salt.
Rest chicken 10 minutes before carving. Serve with potatoes and caper chimichurri.

title: Red Curry Hot Wings Rolled in Peanuts
ingredients: 1½ cups packed cilantro leaves and tender stems
3 lb chicken wings (25–30), drumettes and flats separated
1 (4-oz) jar or can red curry paste
steps: Pat wings dry and toss with kosher salt. Arrange on a parchment-lined rimmed baking sheet; leave uncovered at room temperature at least 30 minutes and up to 1½ hours (or refrigerate overnight and bring to room temperature before roasting).

Heat oven to 300°F. Drizzle wings generously with vegetable oil and toss to coat. Bake 25 minutes, then raise temperature to 450°F and roast, turning halfway, another 30–35 minutes until crisp and golden.

While wings roast, heat a little vegetable oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add red curry paste, cover briefly to limit splatter, and cook, shaking pan and stirring as needed, until darkened and beginning to stick, about 2 minutes.
Whisk in coconut milk and honey. Simmer gently, whisking, until thickened enough to coat a spoon, 10–12 minutes. Taste and add red pepper flakes if desired; keep warm.
Finely chop peanuts and cilantro; halve limes. Toss hot cooked wings with coconut-curry glaze, peanuts and cilantro. Squeeze over lime juice and toss again. Serve with remaining lime halves.

notes: Original recommends seasoning wings well ahead of roasting. Total time estimated, including 30-minute seasoning rest. Chicken wings should reach at least 165°F.

title: One-Pot Chicken Mujadara
ingredients: 2½ cups plain whole-milk yogurt (not Greek), plus more to serve
6 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided, plus more to serve
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 cup long-grain white rice, such as jasmine or basmati
1 cup dried brown or black lentils (not quick-cooking)
1½ tsp salt, for rice and lentils
steps: Place whole chicken in large zip-top bag. Stir yogurt, a few generous glugs of olive oil (about 3 tbsp), 2 tbsp salt, cinnamon, cumin, turmeric and 2 tsp freshly ground black pepper together. Add to bag, massage over chicken and into cavity, seal and refrigerate at least 1 hour and up to 24 hours.
Thinly slice shallots and onions crosswise into ¼-inch rings. Position rack in lower third of oven and preheat to 475°F.

Toss shallots and onions in a large Dutch oven with remaining 3 tbsp olive oil, salt and pepper. Place marinated chicken directly on top, reserving excess marinade. Halve one lemon and tuck both halves into chicken cavity. Drizzle chicken with olive oil, cover and roast 35 minutes.

Mix 3 cups water with reserved marinade and 1½ tsp salt. Rinse rice and lentils together in fine-mesh strainer. Remove Dutch oven from oven; lift chicken to one side and pour rice and lentils around it. Add water-marinade mixture, stir to distribute, and cover.
Braise 45–55 minutes until rice and lentils are tender and chicken is cooked. Remove from oven and rest covered 10 minutes.
Cut remaining lemons in half. Carve chicken, season lentils to taste, and serve with additional yogurt and lemon halves.

notes: Marinating time is 1–24 hours and is not fully included in estimated total time. For food safety, cook chicken to 165°F and avoid holding raw chicken marinade unless thoroughly cooked as directed.

title: Spicy Green Fregola with Salty Yog
ingredients: ⅔ cup plain whole-milk yogurt (not Greek)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
steps: Bring large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook fregola until al dente according to package directions. Drain in a fine-mesh strainer and rinse under cold water until cool; transfer to a large bowl.
Coarsely chop dill and chiles. Blend with baby spinach, garlic, a large pinch of salt and ⅔ cup olive oil until smooth, about 1 minute. Taste and adjust salt.
Season yogurt with salt in a small bowl; it should taste salted but not overly salty.
Pour green sauce over fregola. Add juice of 1 lemon and stir to coat. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Make a well in center of fregola and spoon in salty yogurt. Sprinkle platter with sesame seeds and freshly cracked black pepper; serve.

nutrition.source: No published nutrition information in photographed recipe; not estimated

notes: Recipe can be served cold or at room temperature. Fregola or pearl couscous may be used. Time estimated.

title: Olive Oil–Drowned Potatoes with Lemony Onions & Herbs
ingredients: 1 bunch tender mixed herbs (cilantro, basil, parsley, dill and/or chives)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
⅓ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
1 cup Diamond Crystal kosher salt, for boiling water
steps: Halve any potatoes larger than your palm. Cover potatoes with water in a large pot, season with 1 cup Diamond Crystal kosher salt (or ¾ cup Morton kosher salt), and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook until tender when pierced with fork but not falling apart. Drain.
While potatoes cook, thinly slice red onion. Put in a medium bowl with a big pinch of salt and juice of ½ lemon; squeeze gently to macerate. Set aside.

While potatoes are still warm, break apart with your hands or crush with bottom of a glass measuring cup into a few pieces. Transfer to serving dish and drizzle with ⅓ cup olive oil; season with salt and plenty of freshly ground black pepper. Add more oil if dry.

Squeeze juice of remaining 1½ lemons over potatoes. Pick herb leaves and toss with lemony onions once or twice; pile on potatoes. Finish with additional black pepper, lemon juice and olive oil to taste.

notes: The unusually high salt quantity is for the potato cooking water, which is drained. Original calls for 1 cup Diamond Crystal or ¾ cup Morton kosher salt. Cooking time estimated.

title: Not So Basic B Turkey Sando
ingredients: 1 head Little Gem lettuce, or a few romaine leaves
1 tbsp sherry vinegar, plus more for drizzling
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
steps: Finely chop 2 tsp drained capers, 1 cup cilantro, 1 cup parsley, and seeded jalapeños; thinly slice 3 scallions. Mix with ½ cup mayonnaise and 1 tbsp sherry vinegar; season with salt and pepper.
Halve the focaccia squares and spread both cut sides with chimichurri mayonnaise. Add thick slices of roasted turkey.
Halve avocado, remove pit, and thinly slice flesh. Layer avocado over turkey, season with salt and pepper, and drizzle with sherry vinegar.
Add Little Gem leaves and a handful of salt-and-vinegar potato chips to each sandwich. Top with remaining focaccia halves, cut in half, and serve.

nutrition.source: Not provided in photographed recipe; not estimated

notes: Time estimated; source gives no numerical total time. May use leftover roast turkey or deli-style roast turkey.

title: Sesame Biscuits with Black Pepper–Miso Gravy
ingredients: 16 tbsp (2 sticks) unsalted butter, cold (12 tbsp for biscuits; 4 tbsp for gravy)
¾ cup buttermilk, plus more for brushing
½ cup (71 g) toasted sesame seeds, divided
2½ cups plus 2 tbsp (315 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment. Cut 12 tbsp cold butter into ½-inch cubes and refrigerate. Put a scant ⅓ cup toasted sesame seeds in a small bowl for coating.

Whisk 2½ cups (300 g) flour with 3 tbsp sesame seeds (26 g), 2 tsp kosher salt, 1¾ tsp baking powder, 1 tsp sugar, and ½ tsp baking soda. Work cold butter into flour with fingers until coarse with some pea-size pieces.
Make a well and add ¾ cup buttermilk and 1 tsp toasted sesame oil; stir into large clumps. Gently knead to bring dough together, then move to floured work surface.

Pat into a 4 × 4-inch rectangle; cut into 4 squares and stack. Press to compress, pat into an 8 × 4-inch rectangle, and cut into 8 squares. Brush tops and bottoms with buttermilk, dip tops into sesame seeds, and sprinkle with flaky salt.

Bake 18–22 minutes until golden. For gravy, heat remaining 4 tbsp butter in cast-iron skillet over medium heat. Brown 1 lb sausage in one layer, 3–4 minutes on first side; break into bite-size pieces and brown 2–3 minutes more; transfer to a plate.
Reduce heat to low. Cook sliced garlic, 3 tbsp white miso, and plenty of freshly ground black pepper in skillet about 30 seconds, until fragrant but not browned.

Stir in remaining 2 tbsp (15 g) flour and cook 1 minute. Gradually whisk in 2 cups whole milk and 1 tbsp soy sauce; raise heat to medium and simmer 3–4 minutes, whisking until thickened. Return sausage to skillet; adjust seasoning.
Split biscuits and spoon sausage gravy over each; finish with flaky sea salt and remaining sesame seeds.

nutrition.source: Not provided in photographed recipe; not estimated

notes: Total time estimated. Recipe is photographed across two consecutive pages. Biscuits can be cut and refrigerated overnight before baking.

title: Griddled Chorizo & Egg Stuffed Pitas
ingredients: ½ cup pickled jalapeños, plus their brine
steps: Finely chop ½ cup pickled jalapeños. Stir into a few generous dollops of sour cream with a splash or two of jalapeño brine; season with salt.
Thinly slice scallions and remove chorizo casings. Cut an X-shaped slit in the top of each pita pocket, taking care not to cut through the bottom layer.

Divide chorizo between pitas, pressing it into an even layer against the bottom. Crack an egg into the center of each pita, tuck pita flaps around egg, season with salt, and scatter sliced scallions on top.
Heat a generous glug of olive oil in large skillet over medium. Brush the top of one pita lightly with oil, set in skillet cut-side down, and cook 4 minutes until deeply browned and crisp.
Flip quickly with a large flat spatula and cook second side 2–3 minutes. Flip again and cook 1–2 minutes longer, until chorizo reaches 155°F (about 8 minutes total). Repeat with second pita.
Season tops with salt, quarter pitas, and serve with jalapeño sour cream.

notes: Time estimated. Use fresh, raw Mexican chorizo, not cured Spanish chorizo. Source specifies 155°F for sausage; for food safety, ground pork sausage is generally recommended to reach 160°F.

title: The One & Only Hoagie
ingredients: ⅓ lb sliced spicy soppressata or salami
¾ cup jarred hot or mild giardiniera, preferably oil-packed
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
steps: Thinly slice iceberg lettuce into shrettuce and thinly slice red onion. Toss with ¾ cup giardiniera, 2 oz grated Parmesan, ¼ cup red wine vinegar, a couple glugs of olive oil, salt, and freshly ground black pepper. Taste and adjust acid and seasoning.
Optional: split rolls lengthwise and toast cut sides under broiler or in toaster oven until golden.
Swipe each side of rolls with a light coating of Calabrian chiles if desired. Divide mortadella, capicola, and spicy soppressata evenly between roll bottoms, draping and folding the slices.
Pile on generous shrettuce slaw, cap with roll tops, and cut in half crosswise. Wrap in parchment or foil if needed to hold together.

title: Bloo Smoo (Blueberry-Ginger Smoothie)
steps: Combine cashew or almond milk, frozen blueberries, ice, frozen banana, pitted date, fresh ginger, vanilla extract, and kosher salt in a blender.
Blend on high until thick and creamy. Serve immediately.

title: Tahini Date Shake Smoo
steps: Combine all ingredients in a blender. Blend on high until thick and creamy; serve immediately.

title: Black Sesame Rice Pudding Brûlée
ingredients: 7 large eggs (6 yolks plus 1 whole egg)
Kosher salt (2 teaspoons in the custard)
1¼ cups sugar, divided (¾ cup for custard; ½ cup for brûlée)
steps: Place an oven rack in the bottom third of the oven, remove other racks, and preheat to 325°F. Place a 9-inch round cake pan in a deep skillet with room around it for a water bath.

Boil a small pot of salted water; add ½ cup rice and cook until nearly tender but still slightly undercooked, about 8 minutes. Drain and place rice in the cake pan. Coarsely crush the black sesame seeds.
Heat cream and milk in a saucepan over medium-low until just simmering, then turn off heat.
Whisk 6 egg yolks and 1 whole egg together in a large bowl. Whisk in ¾ cup sugar, tahini, vanilla, 2 teaspoons salt, cinnamon, cardamom and crushed sesame seeds.
While whisking continuously, temper the egg mixture with the hot cream a little at a time, then add the rest gradually.
Pour custard over the rice. Fill the surrounding skillet with hot tap water until the water reaches about three-quarters of the cake-pan sides. Bake 38–42 minutes until set but still jiggly.
Cool at room temperature 20 minutes, then refrigerate at least 4 hours.

Position rack at least 6 inches from broiler and preheat broiler. Sprinkle the remaining ½ cup sugar evenly over custard. Broil on a rimmed sheet, watching and rotating, until deeply caramelized, 2–6 minutes. Cool or serve immediately.
notes: Use ¾ cup sugar in the custard and the remaining ½ cup for the brûlée topping (1¼ cups total). Total time is an estimate including at least 4 hours of chilling.

title: Orange Creamsicle Poppy Cake
ingredients: 2 oranges, preferably blood oranges (zest and juice)
½ cup (100 g) neutral oil, such as canola or vegetable, plus more for pan
2 teaspoons kosher salt, divided (1½ teaspoons batter; ½ teaspoon swirl)
1 cup plus 2 tablespoons (223 g) granulated sugar
⅔ cup plus 2 tablespoons (114 g) poppy seeds, divided (⅔ cup swirl; 2 tablespoons topping)
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease a 9 × 5-inch loaf pan and line with parchment, leaving overhang on both long sides.
Whisk flour, baking powder and 1½ teaspoons kosher salt in a medium bowl.
Finely grate zest of both oranges into a large bowl with the granulated sugar; rub together with fingers. Whisk in eggs, then ¾ cup (170 g) sour cream, juice of both oranges, oil and vanilla.
Whisk dry ingredients into wet ingredients just until incorporated; set aside.
Finely grind ⅔ cup (96 g) poppy seeds in a blender or spice grinder. Transfer to the bowl used for flour; mix in remaining 1 cup (227 g) sour cream, powdered sugar and remaining ½ teaspoon salt.

Pour half the cake batter into the prepared pan. Add half the poppy cream in a central stripe, away from pan sides. Add remaining batter and poppy cream. Swirl about five times with an offset spatula or spoon, allowing some cream to sink.
Scatter remaining 2 tablespoons poppy seeds over the top. Bake 50–55 minutes, until cake springs back and a toothpick inserted in center comes out clean (avoiding pockets of poppy cream).
Cool until pan is safe to handle; lift cake out by parchment and finish cooling on a wire rack before slicing.
notes: Time is estimated; source specifies a 50–55 minute bake.

title: Broiled & Burnt Roasted Tomato Soup with Grilled Cheese Crostini
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper
6 cups vegetable stock, chicken stock, or water
Crostini: 1 baguette, cut into ¼-inch slices
¼ cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese
steps: Preheat broiler on low. Toss tomatoes, onion, jalapeños and smashed garlic with olive oil, salt and pepper on a baking sheet. Broil 30 minutes, tossing every 10 minutes, until pleasantly charred.
Leave broiler on and increase to high. Transfer charred vegetables to a large Dutch oven, add tomato purée and stock, bring to a rolling boil, then simmer over low heat for 30 minutes.
Toast baguette slices, then rub each with the peeled garlic clove. Top with mozzarella and cheddar. Arrange on a baking sheet and broil approximately 2 minutes, watching carefully until melted.
Purée the soup until smooth. Serve with grilled-cheese crostini.
notes: The cookbook calls this “Broiled and Burnt Roasted Tomato Soup with Grilled Cheese Crostini Thing.” Printed prep time: 1 hour 15 minutes.

title: Irish Lamb Stew
ingredients: 2 pounds lamb shoulder, cut into 2-inch chunks
Half of a 750 mL bottle full-bodied red wine
Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper
steps: In a large Dutch oven over medium heat, cook bacon until crispy; remove with a slotted spoon, leaving fat behind.
Coat lamb chunks with tomato paste. Brown lamb in batches in the bacon fat, about 10 minutes total, and set aside with bacon. Preheat oven to 325°F.
Cook onion in the pot until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook 1 minute. Sprinkle flour over onions and garlic; stir and cook 1–2 minutes to remove raw flour taste.
Pour in Guinness and red wine, scraping the pot bottom to loosen browned bits. Simmer until liquid reduces by half, about 20 minutes.

Return lamb and bacon to pot with carrots, potatoes, turnips, 3 cups beef stock, bay leaves and thyme. Season with 1 tablespoon each salt and pepper as directed in source. Bring to a boil, cover and transfer to oven.
Roast 2–2½ hours until lamb is fork-tender. Stir occasionally and add additional beef stock as necessary to keep a thick, soupy consistency.
Let stew cool slightly, remove thyme stems and bay leaves, adjust seasoning, and serve hot with buttered bread.
notes: Printed prep time is 4 hours; actual total time may vary. The recipe uses beer and wine; alcohol may remain after cooking.

title: Gumbo
ingredients: ¾ cup vegetable oil, plus more for cooking
12 oz chorizo or andouille sausage, sliced ½ inch thick
1 lb tiger shrimp, tails on, shelled
2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper
steps: In a Dutch oven, heat ¾ cup oil over medium-high. Stir in flour until smooth. Reduce to medium-low and stir constantly until roux is deep brown like milk chocolate, 30–60 minutes; start over if it burns. Remove from heat and set aside.

In another large Dutch oven, brown sliced sausage over medium-high, about 5 minutes; remove. Quickly sear shrimp on both sides and remove. Add a little oil if needed, then cook chicken about 10 minutes until no longer pink; remove.

Reduce heat to medium. Cook onion, bell pepper and celery until tender, 5–7 minutes. Add garlic, bay leaves, thyme, oregano, paprika and cayenne; cook 2–3 minutes. Stir in tomatoes and stock and bring to a gentle simmer.

Return roux pot to medium heat. Gradually ladle hot soup into roux, stirring vigorously to prevent lumps. Once incorporated, add sausage and chicken. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered 30–60 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add okra about 20 minutes before serving and continue simmering. Add shrimp for the final 8–10 minutes. Season to taste, discard bay leaves and serve with cooked rice.
notes: The source labels the total as “prep time: 3 hours.” The roux may take 30–60 minutes; never leave it unattended.

title: Beef Noodle Soup
ingredients: 1 lb dried white wheat noodles, medium-thick
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Blanch beef for 4 minutes; drain, rinse under cold water and remove impurities.

In a clean large pot, heat oil over medium. Cook onion, garlic and ginger until golden, about 4 minutes. Add doubanjiang and stir until lightly caramelized, about 1 minute. Add cinnamon, star anise and bay leaves; cook until aromatic.

Add rice wine and reduce by half. Stir in soy sauce, rock sugar and water; bring to a boil. Return beef, cover and simmer over low heat until tender enough to pierce with a knife but not falling apart, about 2 hours. Skim surface as needed.

Cook noodles separately until tender and chewy; drain. Remove beef and strain broth through a fine-mesh strainer, discarding solids. Return strained broth and beef to pot, gently simmer and season with salt.
Slice beef into ½-inch pieces. Serve beef, broth and noodles with bok choy, scallions, cilantro and chili crisp arranged for diners to add as desired.
notes: The source lists 2½ hours preparation. Bok choy is served among the toppings; the photographed directions do not specify a separate cooking step for it.

title: Peaches with Goat Cheese, Mint, Honeycomb & Olive Oil
ingredients: Maple walnuts: ½ cup maple syrup
½ cup All the Herbs Salsa Verde (separate source recipe, page 334)
Maldon salt and freshly cracked black pepper
steps: Line a baking sheet with parchment. In a small pot over medium-high, melt maple syrup and sugar together and bring to a bubble. When bubbles reach about 1 inch and mixture thickens and caramelizes, vigorously stir in walnuts. Transfer to prepared sheet and cool completely; chop.
Heat a grill very hot. Sear peaches and lemon halves cut-side down about 30 seconds per side, working quickly so fruit does not collapse. Cool to room temperature, then quarter peaches.

Dollop salsa verde in six spots on a platter. Place peach pieces cut-side up over salsa verde. Add chunks of goat cheese, ½ tsp chopped maple walnuts per peach, honeycomb, mint, parsley, Maldon salt and pepper. Finish with olive oil and serve with grilled lemon.
notes: Calls for “All the Herbs Salsa Verde” on source cookbook page 334; its recipe is not present here. The maple walnut recipe makes more than is used for this salad.

title: Spaghetti with Mint, Ricotta & Olive Oil–Baked Bread Crumbs
ingredients: ¼ loaf Italian bread, cut into croutons
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to coat pasta
Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper
steps: Heat oven to 400°F. Toss bread cubes with ¼ cup olive oil, garlic powder, salt and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast 15–20 minutes until crunchy. Cool, then pulse into crumbs in a food processor.
Whisk three-quarters of ricotta with lemon zest, lemon juice and buttermilk until loose enough to coat the back of a spoon; reserve remaining ricotta for plating.
Cook spaghetti in salted boiling water until al dente, about 8 minutes. Drain and transfer to a baking sheet; toss with olive oil to prevent sticking.

Mix bread crumbs, chile flakes, chives and black pepper in a bowl. Dollop reserved ricotta onto four plates. Coat spaghetti with whipped ricotta and twirl portions in bread-crumb mixture. Place pasta over ricotta and finish with lemon supremes and chopped mint.
notes: The printed ingredients list both “1 lemon, cut into segments” and “1 lemon, supremed”; plating specifically calls for lemon supremes. Source describes this as a composed spaghetti salad.

title: Vasos de Fruta
ingredients: ¼ large watermelon, cut into 1-inch pieces
½ cup Thai basil leaves, chopped
2 tsp Tajín, plus more to serve
Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper
steps: Combine pineapple, mango, watermelon and dragon fruit in a large bowl.
In another bowl, mix serrano, Thai basil, honey, lime zest and juice, chamoy and Tajín. Season with salt to taste.
Pour dressing over fruit and toss gently. Cover and refrigerate at least 30 minutes to meld flavors. Toss again before serving; add extra Tajín and freshly cracked black pepper.
notes: Source specifies 40 minutes preparation including at least 30 minutes of chilling.

title: Warm Potato Salad
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper
Creamy dip: ¼ cup cream cheese
Creamy dip: 2 tbsp whole-grain Dijon mustard, plus 1 tsp for garnish
steps: Simmer potatoes in cold salted water until fork-tender, 15–20 minutes; drain and cool slightly.
Combine cream cheese and 2 tbsp mustard for creamy dip.
Gently smash potatoes with bottom of clean pot. Brown in melted butter over medium heat, 5–10 minutes per side; transfer with butter to bowl.
Cook bacon lardons in cast-iron skillet over low heat until desired crispness; drain.
Toss potatoes with vinegar, 2 tbsp mustard, bacon, diced red onion, scallions, parsley, chives, dill, salt and pepper. Break large potatoes into smaller pieces as needed.
Top with creamy dip, remaining 1 tsp mustard and pickled red onion. Drizzle with olive oil and finish with Maldon salt.

title: Stracciatella di Bufala, Caponata, Sun-Dried Tomatoes, Cherry Peppers & Basil
ingredients: 4 pickled cherry bomb peppers, seeded and sliced
2 cups chopped sun-dried tomatoes in olive oil
Maldon salt and freshly cracked black pepper
steps: Preheat broiler to high. Slice focaccia horizontally; drizzle insides with olive oil and broil until golden, 3–5 minutes.
Mix pickled cherry bomb peppers and sun-dried tomatoes with 1 tbsp of sun-dried tomato oil.
Spread half the stracciatella on each focaccia half; season with Maldon salt and black pepper.
On bottom half, add tomato-pepper mixture and basil; spread caponata over it. Close, cut into quarters and serve.

title: Fried Shrimp Po’Boy
ingredients: 8 oz tiger shrimp, peeled and deveined
½ cup finely sliced yellow onion
steps: Mix smoked paprika, white pepper, oregano, garlic powder, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp Old Bay and buttermilk. Add shrimp and marinate 1 hour.
In separate bowl combine flour, cornmeal, remaining 1 tsp salt and remaining 1 tsp Old Bay.
Heat 4 inches canola oil in large saucepan to 350°F; adjust heat to maintain temperature. Line plate with paper towels.
Lift shrimp individually from marinade, coat completely with flour mixture and fry in batches, turning halfway, about 2 minutes until golden and crisp. Drain.
Halve rolls; spread insides with mayonnaise and butter. Layer lettuce, tomatoes, onion, pickles and fried shrimp. Serve immediately.

title: Buffalo Chicken Finger
ingredients: Chicken fingers: 2 boneless, skinless chicken breasts
Hot sauce: 1 cup hot sauce (preferably Frank’s RedHot), plus more for serving
Hot sauce: ½ cup unsalted butter, melted
Hot sauce: ½ tsp freshly cracked black pepper
Blue cheese sauce: ¼ cup crumbled blue cheese
Blue cheese sauce: ¼ cup sour cream
Blue cheese sauce: ½ cup mayonnaise
Blue cheese sauce: 1 tbsp lemon juice
½ head iceberg lettuce, thinly sliced, for serving
½ cup white onion, thinly sliced, for serving
½ cup hot pickled banana peppers, for serving
¼ cup bread-and-butter pickles, for serving
steps: Slice each chicken breast lengthwise into 3 strips; season generously with salt.
Set out flour, beaten eggs and bread crumbs in separate dishes. Coat chicken in flour, egg and bread crumbs.
Heat at least 2 inches oil in deep skillet over medium-high to 350°F. Fry chicken in batches until golden and cooked through, about 3 minutes per side.
Mix hot sauce, melted butter, 1 tsp salt and black pepper. Dip cooked strips in sauce and set on wire rack.
Mix 2 tbsp blue cheese with sour cream, mayonnaise and lemon juice until smooth; reserve remaining 2 tbsp blue cheese for topping.

Split buns and remove some interior bread from top halves. Spread bottom halves with blue cheese sauce. Layer lettuce, tomato, onion, banana peppers, pickles, remaining blue cheese and chicken. Add more sauce if desired; close and serve.

title: Cubano
ingredients: Roasted pork: ¼ cup orange juice
Roasted pork: 2 tbsp light brown sugar
Roasted pork: ½ tsp freshly cracked black pepper
Roasted pork: ½ tsp smoked paprika
Roasted pork: ½ tsp ground cumin
steps: Mix olive oil, orange juice, lime juice, brown sugar, salt, pepper, paprika, cumin and garlic. Score pork shoulder; rub with marinade in a large resealable bag and refrigerate overnight.

Heat oven to 325°F. Place drained pork in large roasting pan, pour Coca-Cola around it and cover tightly with foil. Roast about 2 hours, basting every 30 minutes, until tender and easily pulled apart.
Remove foil, raise oven to 400°F and roast 15–20 minutes more to form golden crust. Rest at least 30 minutes before slicing or shredding. Reserve 8 oz for sandwiches.
Heat oven to 300°F and preheat griddle or panini press over medium heat. Slice bread horizontally; spread mustard on bottom and mayonnaise on top.
Layer pork, ham, Swiss and lengthwise-sliced pickles. Close sandwiches and butter outsides.
Press sandwiches on griddle or panini press until bread is toasted and cheese melts, 5–10 minutes per side. Finish in oven for 10 minutes to melt cheese fully. Slice diagonally.

title: Muffuletta
ingredients: Olive salad: 1 cup pitted green olives
½ cup peeled roasted Calabrian chili peppers
½ cup peeled roasted red peppers
steps: Pulse olives, celery, garlic, Calabrian peppers, roasted red peppers, parsley, oil, vinegar, oregano, and black pepper in a blender to a chunky consistency. Marinate at least 10 minutes.
Slice bread horizontally, removing some soft interior if desired. Spread one-third of olive salad on the bottom half.
Layer ham, half the provolone, capicola, another third of olive salad, sweet coppa, mozzarella, soppressata, mortadella, Genoa salami, remaining provolone, and remaining olive salad.
Press down and let stand 15 minutes; slice into four wedges.

title: Not a Jos Louis
ingredients: Cream cheese filling: 1 pound cream cheese, room temperature
steps: Beat cream cheese and powdered sugar with stand-mixer paddle on medium until smooth. Slowly add melted butter while mixing; scrape bowl and chill filling.
Bake chocolate cake mix according to package directions in a 9-by-13-inch pan at least 2 inches deep; cool to room temperature.
Cut 4-inch circles from cake with ring mold, then slice each circle horizontally into ½-inch-thick rounds.
Melt dark chocolate, cocoa butter, and chocolate chips in a bowl over simmering water, stirring until smooth, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat; cool until warm and pourable.
Pipe cream cheese filling between pairs of cake rounds. Set sandwiches on a wire rack over a baking sheet, pour chocolate glaze over them, and let coating set.

title: Fluffernutter on Wonder Bread with Peanut Butter and Chocolate Chips Microwaved for 10-Second Sandwich
ingredients: 2 tablespoons Marshmallow Fluff (or another marshmallow crème)
steps: Spread Marshmallow Fluff edge to edge on one slice of bread. Spread peanut butter on the other slice.
Scatter chocolate chips evenly over peanut butter and press them down lightly. Close sandwich with marshmallow side on top.
Microwave on a plate on high for 10 seconds. Eat immediately while warm.

title: Classic Ice Cream Sandwich
ingredients: Assembly: 12 York Peppermint Chocolate Chip Cookies (recipe below)
Assembly: 4 cups Mint Chocolate Chip Ice Cream (recipe below)
Cookies: ½ cup unsalted butter, softened
Cookies: ¾ cup packed light brown sugar
Cookies: one 3.5-ounce dark chocolate bar (78% cacao), cut into chunks
Ice cream: green food coloring, optional
Ice cream: 1 cup dark chocolate curls or chopped dark chocolate
steps: Cookies: Preheat oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet. Whisk flour, baking powder, and baking soda.
Cream butter with granulated and brown sugars until light, about 1 minute. Add salt, egg, egg yolk, and vanilla; mix 2–3 minutes. Gradually add dry ingredients and fold in chocolate chunks.
Scoop dough into 12 portions using a 2-ounce scoop. Flatten a portion, center a York Peppermint Patty, and wrap dough around to enclose. Repeat; space cookies about 2 inches apart.
Bake cookies until edges are golden, 10–12 minutes. Sprinkle with Maldon salt; cool completely on a rack.
Ice cream: Warm milk to a gentle simmer. Whisk egg yolks and sugar until smooth. Slowly whisk hot milk into yolks to temper.

Return custard to saucepan over low heat; stir until slightly thickened and coats the back of a spoon. Strain into bowl, then mix in cream, peppermint and vanilla extracts, and optional green food coloring.
Cool and refrigerate custard at least 4 hours or overnight. Churn in an ice cream maker according to manufacturer instructions, adding dark chocolate during final minutes. Freeze overnight.
Assembly: Scoop ice cream onto flat side of six cooled cookies. Press remaining six cookies on top; freeze sandwiches until firm, at least 1–2 hours.

notes: Cookie and ice cream component recipes are fully included. Total time includes overnight chilling/freezing; estimate.

title: Anything Pesto
ingredients: 3 ounces (about 4 heaping cups/85 g) fresh leafy herbs and/or greens, such as basil, parsley, mint, dill, chives, spinach, destemmed kale, or arugula
½ cup plus 2 tablespoons (150 ml) olive oil, plus more as needed
⅓ cup (35 g) freshly grated pecorino Romano
Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper, to taste
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and prepare a large ice bath.
Blanch herbs and greens in boiling water for 30 seconds, then immediately transfer to ice bath.
Squeeze out excess moisture and roughly chop. Blend with olive oil, pine nuts, lemon zest, and garlic until fairly smooth; add more oil one tablespoon at a time as needed.
Transfer pesto to bowl and fold in pecorino Romano; season with salt and pepper.
Serve or refrigerate in an airtight container up to 5 days.

nutrition.source: Not provided in photographed recipe; not estimated

notes: Preparation time is an estimate.

title: (Almost) Any-Berry, Any-Herb Jam
ingredients: 2 lb (907 g) fresh or frozen berries (blueberries, raspberries, blackberries, or quartered strawberries)
2 tbsp chopped hearty herbs (rosemary, thyme, tarragon, or sage)
1 lemon, halved and juiced (reserve squeezed halves)
steps: Combine berries, sugar, herbs, lemon juice, squeezed lemon halves, and salt in a large bowl. Cover and refrigerate 8–24 hours to macerate.
Transfer everything, including lemon halves, to a medium pot over medium heat. Stir and mash with a wooden spoon until softly boiling, about 8 minutes.

Reduce heat to medium-low; stir occasionally until berries break down and mixture thickens to 220°F (104°C), 35–45 minutes. Alternatively test a small amount on a freezer-cold plate; it should hold its path when pushed and wrinkle slightly. Skim foam as needed.
Remove from heat and cool to room temperature; discard lemon halves.
Serve or refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 months.

nutrition.source: Not provided in photographed recipe; not estimated

notes: Suggested combinations: blackberry–rosemary, blueberry–sage, raspberry–tarragon, strawberry–thyme. The cookbook also suggests adding a dried bay leaf.

title: Spicy Chicken-Salt Sesame Crackers
ingredients: Cracker dough: 1¼ cups (163 g) all-purpose flour
¼ cup (45 g) semolina flour, plus more for dusting
Chicken salt: 1½ tsp chicken bouillon powder
½ tsp freshly cracked black pepper
steps: Whisk all-purpose flour, semolina, yeast, and salt. Add beaten egg and water; mix into shaggy dough and knead about 3 minutes until stiff and cohesive.
Return dough to bowl, cover, and rest at room temperature for 1 hour; it will rise only slightly.
Whisk chicken bouillon powder, nutritional yeast, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, pepper, cayenne, and celery seeds in a small bowl.
Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C) with rack centered; line a baking sheet with parchment.
Working with half the dough at a time, roll with pasta machine or rolling pin to about ⅛ inch (3 mm) thick, dusting with semolina as needed.
Drizzle lined tray with olive oil, place first dough sheet on tray, and brush with more oil.
Sprinkle generously with sesame seeds and half the chicken salt; prick all over with fork. Cover with parchment and another baking sheet.
Bake 20 minutes. Remove top tray and parchment; bake another 8–10 minutes until crisp and golden. Cool on wire rack.
Repeat with remaining dough.
Break cooled crackers into irregular pieces. Store airtight at room temperature for up to 3 days.

notes: With four matching baking sheets, both crackers can be rolled and baked at once on upper and lower oven racks.

title: Butter Bean, Sungold, and Smashed Cucumber Salad
ingredients: 2 mini seedless cucumbers, smashed and cut into irregular ½-inch (1 cm) chunks
3 tbsp celery vinegar or red wine vinegar
Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper, to taste
1 (15.5-oz / 439 g) can butter beans, drained and rinsed
⅓ cup (80 ml) extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving
1 red finger chile or Fresno chile, thinly sliced
¼ cup (8 g) loosely packed torn fresh basil leaves
steps: Toss tomatoes, smashed cucumbers, vinegar, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl. Let marinate at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Add drained butter beans, olive oil, scallions, chile, and basil; toss and adjust salt and pepper.
Serve with additional olive oil and pepper.

title: Chicken Fat Mashed Potatoes
ingredients: Skin from 4 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs
Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper, to taste
3 lb (1.3 kg) russet potatoes (about 4), scrubbed, peeled, and cut into 2-inch chunks
¼ cup (57 g) unsalted butter, cubed
Thinly sliced fresh chives, to taste
steps: Arrange chicken skins in single layer in medium nonstick pan; add water and cook over medium-low heat, flipping occasionally, until water evaporates and skins render and crisp, 30–35 minutes.
Transfer skins to wire rack or paper towels, salt, and cool completely.
Strain and reserve rendered chicken fat.
Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C); line baking sheet with parchment.
Cover potatoes and garlic with water in a medium pot; bring to boil, salt generously, reduce to medium, and simmer until very tender, 14–16 minutes.
Warm cream, milk, and butter in a small saucepan over low heat until butter melts.
Drain potatoes and garlic and transfer to prepared baking sheet; reserve pot.
Bake potatoes and garlic 6–8 minutes to dry them slightly.
Return to pot and mash with potato masher, or rice in batches for a smoother texture.
Stir in warm dairy mixture and 2–3 tbsp reserved chicken fat. Season with salt and pepper.
Break crispy chicken skins into shards.
Serve mash topped with crispy skins, chives, and more pepper.

notes: The cookbook suggests saving extra rendered chicken fat refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.

title: Spicy Carrot Rigatoni
ingredients: Pasta: 1 lb (454 g) carrots (6–8 medium), peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces; reserve green tops
½ cup (55 g) grated pecorino Romano, plus more for serving
1 tbsp chopped jarred Calabrian chiles in oil
Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper, to taste
Topping: ¼ cup (20 g) finely chopped reserved carrot tops
¼ cup (15 g) finely chopped fresh parsley
Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper, to taste
steps: Set up a steamer over gently boiling water.
Steam carrots and garlic, covered, until very tender, 12–15 minutes.

Blend steamed carrots and garlic with pecorino, ½ cup olive oil, ¼ cup water, Calabrian chiles, and pine nuts until completely smooth. Vent blender lid for hot ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring a large pot of water to boil.
Mix carrot tops, parsley, ¼ cup olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, salt, and pepper for topping.
Salt boiling water and cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving at least 2 mugs of pasta water; return pasta to pot over low heat.
Add carrot sauce and a couple splashes of pasta water, tossing and adding more water until pasta is evenly coated with a loose, silky sauce. Season to taste.
Serve with herby topping, optional ricotta, black pepper, and extra pecorino.

title: Mustardy Herb-Buttered Potatoes
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper, to taste
steps: Cover potatoes with water in a large pot, bring to a boil, salt generously, then reduce to a simmer. Cook until just tender, 12–15 minutes.
Drain potatoes in a colander.
Dry pot over low heat; melt butter and stir in both mustards and honey until smooth.
Remove from heat. Add potatoes, dill, chives, and parsley; gently toss to coat.
Season with salt and pepper and serve.

title: Vegetable Stock
ingredients: 3 small leeks, roots trimmed, cleaned and roughly chopped
2 heads garlic, halved crosswise (skins and all)
1 bunch fresh parsley, roughly chopped (stems and all)
1 small fennel bulb, quartered, with stems and fronds roughly chopped
steps: Add all ingredients to an 8-quart stockpot. Bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce to low and simmer uncovered for 1 hour.
Prepare a large ice bath.
Strain through a fine-mesh strainer into another pot or container; discard solids. Place container over ice bath to cool quickly.
Ladle cooled stock into quart containers and refrigerate to chill completely.
Refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze up to 4 months.

notes: Allow additional time for cooling and chilling.

title: Chicken Broth
ingredients: 2 heads garlic, halved crosswise (skins and all)
1 small fennel bulb, quartered, stems and fronds roughly chopped
1 bunch fresh parsley, roughly chopped (stems and all)
steps: Place chicken wings, feet, and water in a 12-quart stockpot. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, and simmer uncovered for 2 hours, skimming surface as needed. Add water if needed to keep chicken submerged.
Add celery, onions, garlic, fennel, parsley, mushrooms, bay leaves, chile, and peppercorns; barely simmer for 2 more hours.
Prepare a large ice bath. Remove large solids and strain broth through a fine-mesh strainer into a clean container. Cool rapidly over ice bath.
Divide into quart containers and refrigerate until completely chilled.
Refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze up to 4 months.

nutrition.source: Not provided in photographed recipe; not estimated

notes: Chicken feet contribute gelatin; more wings may be substituted. Allow additional time for cooling.

title: Beef Stock
ingredients: 2 heads garlic, halved crosswise (skins and all)
1 bunch fresh parsley, roughly chopped (stems and all)
steps: Preheat oven to 450°F. Roast bones on two sheet trays for 45–60 minutes until deeply golden.
Transfer bones to a 12-quart stockpot. Pour off rendered fat from hot trays; deglaze with a splash of water, scraping browned bits into the stockpot. Add 6 quarts water.
Bring to a boil, reduce to low, and simmer uncovered for 8–12 hours, skimming as needed and adding water to keep bones submerged.
Add celery, garlic, onions, parsley, thyme, bay leaves, chile, and peppercorns; simmer 1 more hour.
Prepare a large ice bath. Remove bones and vegetables, strain through a fine-mesh strainer into another container, and cool rapidly over ice.
Divide into quart containers and chill completely; refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze up to 4 months.

nutrition.source: Not provided in photographed recipe; not estimated

notes: The cookbook specifies 8–12 hours of bone simmering PLUS one additional hour with aromatics; total time is approximate and excludes cooling.

title: Midwestern Fish Fry
ingredients: TARTAR SAUCE: ¼ cup loosely packed chopped fresh dill
¼ cup loosely packed chopped fresh parsley
Zest and juice of ½ lemon
Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste
SLAW: 4 heaping cups (260 g) thinly sliced red cabbage
1 bunch red radishes (about 8), trimmed and thinly sliced
½ small red onion, thinly sliced and rinsed
Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste
FISH: canola oil, for deep frying
¾ cup (100 g) plus ½ cup (65 g) all-purpose flour, divided
½ cup (65 g) medium rye flour
One 12-oz (335 ml) can cold lager-style beer
Four 4–5 oz cod fillets, pin bones and skin removed
Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste
Flake salt and lemon wedges, for serving
steps: Make tartar sauce: blend dill, parsley, egg, garlic, lemon zest, and juice in a high-sided container with immersion blender. Slowly stream in 1 cup canola oil until emulsified. Stir in cornichons, capers, and mustard; season.
Make slaw: toss cabbage, radishes, onion, vinegar, honey, and caraway seeds in a large bowl. Season and refrigerate while preparing fish.
Add 2 inches canola oil to a large pot; attach a candy thermometer and heat over medium-high to 365°F.
Make batter: whisk ¾ cup all-purpose flour, rye flour, and baking powder in a large bowl. Whisk in cold beer until combined; a few lumps are fine. Refrigerate until needed.
Put remaining ½ cup all-purpose flour in a shallow dish. Pat cod dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.

One fillet at a time, dredge in flour, shake off excess, dip fully in batter, and shake off excess. Carefully lower into hot oil, holding for a few seconds before releasing to prevent sticking. Repeat with a second fillet.
Fry until golden and crispy on both sides, flipping halfway, 5–6 minutes. Keep oil around 365°F. Transfer to wire rack or paper-lined plate and sprinkle with flake salt.
Repeat battering and frying with remaining fillets. Serve with tartar sauce, slaw, and lemon wedges.

nutrition.source: Not provided in photographed recipe; not estimated

notes: Contains a homemade raw-egg emulsified tartar sauce; pasteurized egg is recommended for food safety. Deep-fry carefully. Source photo includes both pages of the spread.

title: Salmon Tartare with Potato Chips
ingredients: 1 small Meyer lemon, seeded and minced (regular lemon may substitute)
Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper, to taste
Potato chips: 2 large russet potatoes (about 10 oz/283 g each), skin on, scrubbed and sliced paper-thin
steps: Dice salmon very small and refrigerate until ready to mix.
Rinse potato slices in cold water 3–4 times until water runs clear.
Cover potato slices with cold water by about 1 inch, add vinegar, bring to a boil and immediately strain. Spread on paper-towel-lined trays and pat completely dry.
Heat 1½ inches canola oil to 350°F. Fry chips in three batches, maintaining 350°F, until lightly golden and crisp, about 3–4 minutes. Drain and salt immediately.
Combine chile, lemon, shallot, chives, capers, olive oil and fish sauce. Fold in chilled salmon; season with salt and pepper.
Serve tartare immediately with potato chips.

notes: Use properly handled fish intended for raw consumption; raw fish carries foodborne illness risk. Keep chilled until serving. Source suggests store-bought kettle chips as a shortcut.

title: Roast Chicken with Red Wine Vinegar and Honey
ingredients: 4 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
5 large shallots (about 1 lb/454 g), peeled and halved
Torn fresh parsley leaves, to taste
steps: A day ahead, spatchcock chicken: remove backbone, turn breast side up and press flat. Set on wire rack over sheet pan.
Coarsely grind peppercorns and fennel; mix with porcini powder, salt, oregano and paprika. Reserve 2 tbsp spice mixture for sauce.
Season chicken with remaining rub and refrigerate uncovered 8–24 hours.
Preheat oven to 400°F. Heat olive oil in 12-inch cast-iron pan over medium. Place chicken skin-side down and press with another heavy pan; sear 7–10 minutes until golden.
Remove top pan, flip chicken and sear 2 more minutes; transfer chicken breast-side up to tray.
Sear shallots cut-side down 5–6 minutes until deeply charred. Set chicken breast-side up over shallots and roast 40–50 minutes until breast reaches 160°F and thighs at least 180°F.
Rest chicken at least 15 minutes, up to 45. Move shallots to platter.

Over medium heat melt butter in pan; stir in garlic and reserved spice mix 3–4 minutes until garlic softens and spices toast. Turn off heat; add vinegar and honey, season with salt. Sauce will be broken.
Cut chicken into pieces; serve with shallots, warm sauce and parsley.

nutrition.source: Not provided in photographed recipe; not estimated

notes: Requires 8–24 hours uncovered dry brining before cooking; total time excludes overnight refrigeration. Roast temperatures are as printed in the source.

title: Pot Roast au Poivre with Charred Onions
ingredients: 1 chuck roast (3½ lb/1.5 kg), tied with butcher’s twine
4 medium yellow onions, peeled and halved
½ cup (120 ml) cognac or brandy
1 small bunch fresh thyme, tied with butcher’s twine
2 tbsp green peppercorns in brine, drained and roughly chopped
½ cup (120 ml) cognac or brandy
Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper, to taste
Thinly sliced fresh chives, to taste
steps: Night before, coarsely crush black peppercorns; mix with shiitake powder and salt. Rub roast all over; refrigerate uncovered on rack 8–24 hours.
Preheat oven to 325°F. Heat olive oil in Dutch oven over medium and sear roast on all sides until deep golden, 5–7 minutes per side. Remove.
Sear halved onions cut-side down 2–3 minutes until deeply charred; add garlic for 1 minute.
Remove pot from heat; deglaze with ½ cup cognac, scraping browned bits. Reduce by half with residual heat, 1–2 minutes.
Return to medium heat; add beef stock, thyme, bay leaves and roast with juices. Liquid should reach halfway up meat; add water if needed.
Cover and bake 3–4 hours until fork tender. Remove meat and cover to keep warm. Remove onions and garlic to a platter.
Strain braising liquid and skim excess fat. Wipe Dutch oven, melt butter over medium, and soften minced shallots 3–4 minutes.
Add green peppercorns. Off heat, deglaze with remaining ½ cup cognac and reduce by half 1–2 minutes.
Add 1½ cups reserved braising liquid; reduce over medium-high until lightly coats a spoon, 6–8 minutes.
Add cream; simmer until sauce coats back of spoon, 4–6 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Spoon over beef, garnish with chives, serve with charred onions.
