notes: Dry-brine uncovered 8–24 hours before cooking; total time excludes this waiting period. Shiitake powder can be made by grinding dried shiitakes.

title: Tina’s Meatballs
ingredients: Meatballs: ½ cup (55 g) finely grated pecorino Romano
1 small yellow onion, grated on large holes of box grater
¼ cup (15 g) finely chopped fresh parsley
½ tsp freshly cracked black pepper
Olive oil, for greasing hands and searing
Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper, to taste
steps: Combine pecorino, panko, eggs, onion, garlic, parsley, salt and pepper. Add beef and pork and gently mix with hands until just combined.
With oiled hands form 16–18 meatballs about 1½ inches wide (35–40 g each).
Coat large pot with olive oil; heat medium-high. Sear meatballs in two batches, 4–5 minutes on first side, 1–2 minutes on other side. They will finish cooking in sauce.
Reduce heat to low; add passata. Add water to jar, shake and pour into pot; scrape browned bits.
Add sugar, Parmesan rinds if using and bay leaf. Season; return meatballs and juices, gently coat in sauce.
Bring to simmer; reduce to low, cover and cook 25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Uncover and cook 10 minutes more. Season, discard bay leaf and serve.

notes: Recipe yields 16–18 meatballs; source suggests serving over 1 lb pasta or with pecorino, basil and focaccia.

title: Sunday Gravy
ingredients: Gravy: 1 lb (454 g) lamb neck bones, cut into 2-inch pieces
Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper
1 batch Tina’s Meatballs (R074), prepared through shaping
1 lb (454 g) hot Italian sausage (4–5 links)
Braciole: ½ cup (55 g) finely grated pecorino Romano
¼ cup (15 g) finely chopped fresh parsley
Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper
8 very thin slices top round steak (1–1½ lb / 454–680 g)
For serving: 1½ lb (680 g) dry pasta, cooked al dente
steps: Season lamb neck bones; sear in olive oil in large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat until golden on all sides, 4–6 minutes per side. Remove.
Cook onions and garlic in same pot 5–6 minutes until softened. Add tomato paste and cook 1–2 minutes until lightly browned.
Add passata, bay leaves, sugar and pepper flakes. Season generously; return lamb bones. Bring to simmer, lower heat and cook uncovered 1 hour, stirring to prevent scorching.
For braciole, mix pecorino, panko, parsley, olive oil, garlic and egg; season.
Season one side of each beef slice; spread thin layer of filling and roll from short end. Secure with two pieces butcher’s twine. Season outside.
In olive-oiled cast-iron pan over medium heat, sear braciole in two batches on all sides until golden, 4–5 minutes per side.
Deglaze pan with ¼ cup water and add drippings to gravy. Simmer braciole in gravy covered over low heat for 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
In cleaned cast-iron pan, sear shaped meatballs in oil 4–5 minutes on first side, then 1–2 minutes other side. Transfer to plate. Deglaze with ¼ cup water; add drippings to gravy.
Sear sausage links in oiled pan on both sides, 3–4 minutes per side; set aside.
After braciole has cooked 2 hours, add meatballs and sausage. Simmer very low, uncovered, about 1 hour until sauce reduces and meats are cooked through.
Cut sausage links into 2-inch pieces and return to gravy. Remove twine from braciole and return. Lamb bones may be removed or left for serving.
Season gravy, remove bay leaves, and serve over al dente pasta with pecorino Romano.

nutrition.source: Not provided in photographed recipe; not estimated

notes: Includes a full batch of Tina’s Meatballs (R074) as a component; source says prepare them through step 2 before searing for gravy. Allow roughly 4½–5 hours for cooking. No nutrition data provided.

title: Crispy Pan-Seared Sea Bass
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: 4 skin-on sea bass fillets (6–8 ounces each), 1–1½ inches thick
steps: Mix 1½ teaspoons salt with sugar. Score each fillet's skin 3–4 times lengthwise, about ½ inch apart, without cutting into the flesh. Season flesh with salt-sugar mixture and skin with remaining ¼ teaspoon salt. Refrigerate skin side up on a rack for 45 minutes.

Pat fish dry. Heat oil in skillet over high until just smoking. Add fish skin down, reduce heat to medium-low, and press gently with spatula for 20–30 seconds. Cook until skin browns and flesh is opaque except for top ¼ inch, 8–14 minutes; lower heat if oil smokes.
Remove pan from heat, flip fillets with two thin spatulas, and let residual heat finish cooking about 30 seconds, until fish registers 125°F. Serve skin side up.

notes: Dry-brining takes 45 minutes. Other skin-on flaky fish 1–1½ inches thick may be used.

title: Green Olive and Orange Pesto
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
steps: Process parsley, olives, almonds, garlic, orange zest and orange juice in a food processor until smooth, scraping down as needed.
With motor running, slowly add olive oil until incorporated. Transfer to bowl, stir in Parmesan, and season with salt and pepper.

title: Arugula and Almond Pesto
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: 4 anchovy fillets, rinsed and patted dry
1 serrano chile, stemmed, seeded and halved lengthwise
steps: Process almonds, garlic, anchovies and serrano in food processor until finely chopped, about 15 seconds, scraping down as needed.
Add arugula, lemon juice, olive oil and salt. Process until smooth, about 30 seconds.

title: Stir-Fried Beef with Green Beans and Shiitakes
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: 2 tablespoons plus 2 teaspoons vegetable oil, divided
8 ounces shiitake mushrooms, stemmed and cut into 1-inch pieces
12 ounces green beans, trimmed and cut into 2-inch lengths
3 scallions, white and light green parts, quartered lengthwise and cut into 1½-inch lengths
steps: Slice steak with grain into 2-inch strips, then thinly against grain (¼ inch). Toss with soy sauce and sugar; marinate 10–60 minutes, then drain. Mix ginger and garlic with 2 teaspoons oil separately.

Heat 1½ teaspoons oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over high until just smoking. Sear half the beef for 1 minute without stirring, then stir-fry about 2 minutes until browned. Remove; repeat with remaining 1½ teaspoons oil and beef.

Add remaining 1 tablespoon oil and mushrooms to skillet. Brown about 2 minutes. Add green beans; stir-fry 3–4 minutes. Add water, cover, reduce heat to medium, and steam about 2 minutes until crisp-tender.
Push vegetables to sides; cook ginger-garlic mixture in center about 30 seconds, then combine with vegetables.
Return beef and juices with scallions. Add teriyaki sauce and toss over heat until coated and sauce thickens, about 30 seconds. Serve.

notes: Freeze flank steak for 15 minutes to make thin slicing easier. Use a 12-inch nonstick skillet with lid.

title: Teriyaki Stir-Fry Sauce
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
steps: Whisk all ingredients together until fully combined.
Use immediately or refrigerate for up to 2 days; whisk again before using.

nutrition.source: No published nutrition information supplied

title: Roasted Salmon Fillets
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: 1 center-cut skin-on salmon fillet (1¾–2 pounds), 1½ inches thick
steps: Place oven rack in lowest position with a rimmed baking sheet on it. Preheat oven to 500°F. Cut salmon crosswise into 4 fillets. Score skin 4–5 times diagonally without cutting flesh. Pat dry, rub with oil, and season with salt and pepper.

Reduce oven to 275°F. Carefully place salmon skin down on hot sheet. Roast 9–13 minutes, until center is still slightly translucent and reaches 125°F for farmed salmon or 120°F for wild salmon (medium-rare). Transfer to plates.

nutrition.source: No published nutrition information supplied

notes: Keep skin on during roasting; remove afterward if desired. Salmon target temperatures here are from the source for medium-rare fish; FDA guidance for fully cooked fish is 145°F.

title: Roasted Side of Salmon
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: 1 center-cut skin-on side of salmon (1¾–2 pounds), 1½ inches thick
steps: Place oven rack at lowest position with a rimmed baking sheet on it; preheat to 500°F. Grind toasted juniper and fennel coarsely and mix with orange zest, sugar, salt and pepper.

Fold a length of heavy-duty aluminum foil 1 foot longer than salmon lengthwise into thirds to make a sling. Score salmon skin 8 times about 3 inches long and 1 inch apart, without cutting flesh. Pat dry, place skin down on foil, and rub flesh with oil and spice mixture.
Reduce oven to 275°F. Transfer salmon on foil sling to preheated sheet. Roast 14–18 minutes until center is slightly translucent and reaches 125°F (farmed) or 120°F (wild), medium-rare.
Use foil sling to transfer to board. Slide thin metal spatula between flesh and skin, hold fish steady, and gently remove foil and skin. Serve.

notes: Toast juniper and fennel in dry skillet over medium heat until fragrant, about 1 minute. The cookbook gives medium-rare temperatures; FDA guidance for fully cooked fish is 145°F.

title: Mango-Mint Salsa
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: 2 ripe but firm mangoes, peeled, pitted and cut into ¼-inch pieces (3 cups)
2 jalapeño chiles, stemmed, seeded and minced
steps: Combine all ingredients in a bowl. Refrigerate for up to 2 days if not serving immediately.

title: Tangerine-Ginger Relish
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
steps: Cut peel and pith from tangerines. Quarter and slice crosswise into ½-inch pieces. Drain in a fine-mesh strainer over bowl for 15 minutes.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon collected juice. Whisk scallion, ginger, lemon juice and olive oil into reserved juice. Fold in tangerines and season with salt and pepper.

title: Chicken Shawarma
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: 1 small head red cabbage (1¼ pounds), cored and very thinly sliced (6 cups)
2 tablespoons lemon juice, plus 1 whole lemon
2½ pounds boneless skinless chicken thighs, trimmed
½ English cucumber, cut into ½-inch dice
steps: Toss cabbage, parsley, ¼ cup olive oil and 1 teaspoon salt; set aside. Separately mix yogurt, lemon juice, garlic, ¾ teaspoon salt and ½ teaspoon pepper; set aside.
Set oven rack 6 inches from broiler and preheat broiler on high. Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil and place wire rack inside.
Pat chicken dry. Toss with paprika, cumin, remaining 2 teaspoons salt, remaining ½ teaspoon pepper and remaining 2 tablespoons oil.
Arrange chicken smooth side down on rack. Halve lemon and place cut side up on rack. Broil until browned and chicken reaches 175°F, 16–20 minutes, rotating pan halfway. Rest 5 minutes.
Slice chicken thinly and squeeze one broiled lemon half over it. Squeeze remaining half over cabbage and toss. Serve chicken and slaw with tomatoes, cucumber, yogurt sauce and warm pita.

notes: For table salt instead of kosher salt, use half the stated salt amount.

title: Yogurt-Tahini Sauce
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
steps: Whisk yogurt, tahini, lemon zest, lemon juice and garlic together. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Grilled Glazed Boneless Chicken Breasts
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: ¼ cup table salt, for brining
4 boneless skinless chicken breasts (6–8 ounces each), trimmed
steps: Dissolve salt and sugar in 1½ quarts cold water. Submerge chicken, cover and refrigerate 30–60 minutes. Remove and pat dry. Mix milk powder and pepper. (Skip brine if using kosher chicken.)

Prepare a two-zone grill. For charcoal: light a large chimney of charcoal, place two-thirds on one side and remaining third on the other; cover with vent open and heat 5 minutes. For gas: preheat all burners on high about 15 minutes, then leave primary burner high and reduce others to medium-high.
Clean and oil grill grate. Sprinkle half milk-powder mixture on one side of breasts, spray lightly with oil, flip and repeat on other side.
Grill chicken smooth side down on hotter area until browned, 2–2½ minutes. Flip, brush with 2 tablespoons glaze and grill another 2–2½ minutes.

Move chicken to cooler side. Brush with 2 tablespoons glaze, cook 2 minutes, then flip and brush two more times, cooking 2 minutes per side. Brush with remaining glaze and cook another 1–3 minutes, until chicken registers 160°F. Rest 5 minutes before serving.

nutrition.source: No published nutrition information supplied

notes: The recipe uses a 160°F pull temperature followed by a 5-minute rest. Verify a safe final temperature (165°F) before serving.

title: Molasses-Coffee Glaze
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
steps: Whisk balsamic vinegar and cornstarch in a small saucepan until dissolved. Whisk in molasses, corn syrup, coffee, garlic and allspice.
Bring to a boil over high heat, stirring constantly, and cook until thickened, about 1 minute. Transfer to bowl.

nutrition.source: No published nutrition information supplied

title: Miso-Marinated Salmon
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
steps: Whisk miso, sugar, sake, and mirin until dissolved. Coat flesh sides of fillets, arrange skin-side down in baking dish, pour remaining marinade over, cover, and refrigerate 6–24 hours.

Set oven rack 8 inches below broiler and preheat broiler. Line wire rack in rimmed baking sheet with foil. Scrape miso off salmon with fingers without rinsing; arrange skin-side down on foil with 1 inch between fillets.

Broil 8–12 minutes until deeply browned and centers register 125°F for farm-raised salmon or 120°F for wild salmon, rotating sheet halfway through and shielding edges with foil if needed. Serve with lemon wedges.

notes: Total time includes minimum 6-hour marination; marinate no longer than 24 hours.

title: Fresh Tomato Sauce
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, divided
steps: Halve tomatoes across equator. Over a fine-mesh strainer set over bowl, squeeze out seeds and jelly, scraping seeds into strainer. Press liquid through, discard seeds, reserve 1 cup strained liquid, and combine remaining liquid in large bowl.
Cut tomatoes into 1½-inch pieces. Blend in 2–3 batches until smooth, 30–45 seconds per batch. Add puree to bowl with remaining strained liquid (about 10 cups total).

Heat 2 tablespoons oil in large saucepan over medium heat. Cook garlic, pepper flakes, and oregano until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add puree and salt; simmer medium-low until reduced to 4 cups, 45–60 minutes.
Off heat, stir in basil, reserved 1 cup strained tomato liquid, and remaining 2 tablespoons oil. Adjust salt. Refrigerate up to 1 week or freeze up to 3 months.

notes: Use ripe in-season tomatoes, not plum tomatoes. Do not thin with pasta water.

title: Classic Marinara Sauce
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: 2 teaspoons minced fresh oregano OR ½ teaspoon dried oregano
steps: Drain tomatoes over a bowl. Open tomatoes and remove seeds and cores; drain 5 minutes. Reserve about 2½ cups tomato juice (add water if needed) and ¾ cup drained tomatoes.

Heat 2 tablespoons oil in large saucepan over medium. Cook onion until soft and lightly browned, 5–7 minutes; add garlic and oregano for 30 seconds. Add remaining drained tomatoes; cook over medium-high until liquid evaporates and tomatoes brown and stick, 10–12 minutes.
Add wine; cook until syrupy, about 1 minute. Add reserved tomato juice, salt, and pepper, scraping browned bits. Simmer until thickened, 8–10 minutes.

Transfer sauce to food processor; add reserved ¾ cup tomatoes and pulse about 8 times for slightly chunky sauce (3–4 pulses for chunkier). Return to saucepan, simmer, add basil and remaining 1 tablespoon oil. Adjust salt, pepper, and sugar. Refrigerate up to 1 week or freeze up to 3 months.

nutrition.source: No published nutrition information supplied

notes: Variations (confirmed from cookbook page 47): Roasted Garlic Marinara Sauce — Omit the 2 minced garlic cloves. Remove outer papery skins from 3 heads of garlic, trim off top thirds, wrap in foil, and roast at 350°F for 1–1¼ hours until golden and very tender. Cool, squeeze out about 6 tablespoons roasted garlic, and add to food processor with sauce in step 4. Vodka Cream Marinara Sauce — Omit red wine. Add ¼ teaspoon red pepper flakes to onion with garlic. Add ½ cup heavy cream and ⅓ cup vodka to skillet with tomato juice in step 3.

title: Chicken and Sausage Gumbo
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs, trimmed
8 ounces andouille sausage, halved lengthwise and sliced ¼ inch thick
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F with rack in middle. Spread flour in a 12-inch skillet and bake, stirring occasionally, until cinnamon brown, 40–55 minutes. Stir more frequently near end. Transfer to bowl to cool.

Heat oil in Dutch oven over medium. Cook onion, bell pepper, and celery until soft, 5–7 minutes. Add thyme, garlic, paprika, bay leaves, cayenne, salt, and pepper; stir 1 minute. Add 2 cups broth and chicken in single layer. Simmer covered on medium-low until chicken is fork-tender, 15–17 minutes; transfer chicken to plate.

Whisk remaining 2 cups broth gradually into toasted flour to make smooth thick paste. Increase gumbo heat to medium and whisk paste into pot gradually, incorporating each addition. Add andouille and simmer uncovered 20–25 minutes until slightly thickened.

Shred cooled chicken into bite-size pieces. Return chicken and scallions to gumbo; remove from heat, add vinegar, and adjust salt. Discard bay leaves. Serve with hot sauce, preferably over white rice. Refrigerate up to 3 days.

nutrition.source: No published nutrition information supplied

notes: Toasted dry roux can be stored airtight at room temperature up to 6 months. Rice not included in ingredient list because it is suggested for serving.

title: Sautéed Chicken Cutlets
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: 4 (6- to 8-ounce) boneless, skinless chicken breasts, trimmed

CHOOSE ONE PAN SAUCE — Apricot-Orange: 1 tablespoon unsalted butter; 1 minced shallot; 2 minced garlic cloves; 1 cup orange juice; 1 peeled, coarsely chopped orange; 1 cup chopped dried apricots; 2 tablespoons minced fresh parsley

OR Mustard-Cider: 2 teaspoons vegetable oil; 1 minced shallot; 1¼ cups apple cider; 2 tablespoons cider vinegar; 2 teaspoons whole-grain mustard; 2 teaspoons minced fresh parsley; 2 tablespoons unsalted butter
steps: Preheat oven to 200°F. Halve chicken breasts horizontally and pound each piece under plastic wrap to even ¼-inch thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in 12-inch skillet over medium-high until just smoking. Cook 4 cutlets without moving until browned, about 2 minutes. Flip and cook second side until opaque, 15–20 seconds. Transfer to heatproof plate; repeat with remaining oil and cutlets. Tent and keep warm in oven; reserve accumulated juices.

APRICOT-ORANGE SAUCE: Add butter to skillet over medium-high. Soften shallot 2 minutes, add garlic for 15 seconds. Add orange juice, chopped orange, and apricots, scraping browned bits. Simmer until thickened, about 4 minutes. Add chicken juices and parsley; season with salt and pepper. Serve over cutlets.

OR MUSTARD-CIDER SAUCE: Off heat, add 2 teaspoons oil and shallot to hot skillet; stir until softened, about 30 seconds. Return to medium-high and add apple cider and cider vinegar; scrape browned bits. Simmer to ½ cup, 6–7 minutes. Add chicken juices. Off heat, stir in mustard and parsley, then whisk in butter 1 tablespoon at a time until glossy. Season and serve immediately.

nutrition.source: No published nutrition information supplied

notes: The two photographed pan sauces are alternative complete accompaniments, not ingredients to use together.

title: Tandoori Chicken with Raita
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: Chicken: ¼ cup lime juice (from 2 limes), divided, plus lime wedges for serving
Chicken: 3 pounds bone-in chicken pieces (split breasts, drumsticks, and thighs), skin removed and trimmed
steps: Prepare raita: Mix 1 cup yogurt, cilantro, and 1 minced garlic clove. Season with salt and cayenne to taste. Refrigerate until serving; it can be made up to 24 hours ahead.

Heat vegetable oil in a 10-inch skillet over medium heat. Cook 6 minced garlic cloves and ginger until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add garam masala, cumin, and chili powder and cook another 30 seconds. Move half the aromatic mixture into a bowl, stir in 1 cup yogurt and 2 tablespoons lime juice, and reserve as the marinade.

In a large bowl, mix the remaining aromatic mixture with the remaining 2 tablespoons lime juice and the salt. Score each piece of chicken with 2 or 3 short cuts, then rub the seasoned mixture over the chicken. Let stand for 30 minutes at room temperature.

Heat oven to 325°F with rack in upper-middle position. Set a wire rack inside a foil-lined rimmed baking sheet. Coat chicken with reserved yogurt marinade and arrange on rack, scored sides down. Discard leftover marinade. Roast until breasts register 125°F and thighs/drumsticks register 130°F, about 15–25 minutes, removing pieces as they reach the indicated temperatures.

Position oven rack 6 inches from broiler and turn broiler to high. Return chicken to rack, scored sides up. Broil 8–15 minutes, until lightly charred and breasts reach 160°F while thighs/drumsticks reach 175°F.
Transfer chicken to a platter, loosely cover with foil, and rest 5 minutes. Serve with raita and lime wedges.

nutrition.source: No published nutrition panel visible; not estimated

notes: Raita is included as a complete accompaniment within this recipe. For very large chicken breasts (about 1 pound each), cut each breast into three pieces. Serve with rice if desired. Time estimate includes 30-minute rest and cooking; actual oven and broiler times vary.

title: Jerk Rub
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
steps: Grind allspice, peppercorns, and thyme coarsely in spice grinder, about 30 seconds.
Transfer to bowl and stir in sugar, garlic powder, mustard, and cayenne.

title: Cajun-Style Rub
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
steps: Grind coriander seeds finely in spice grinder, about 30 seconds.
Transfer to bowl and stir in celery salt, paprika, cayenne, and cinnamon.

title: Cuban-Style Oven-Roasted Pork Shoulder
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: Pork and brine: 1 (7–8-pound) bone-in, skin-on pork picnic shoulder
Pork and brine: 2 cups table salt
Pork and brine: 4 cups orange juice (8 oranges)
Pork and brine: 2 garlic heads, unpeeled cloves separated and crushed
Garlic-citrus paste: 12 garlic cloves, chopped coarse
Garlic-citrus paste: 2 tablespoons distilled white vinegar
Garlic-citrus paste: 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
steps: Cut 1-inch-deep slits about 1 inch long, 2 inches apart, all over pork skin. Dissolve sugar and salt in 6 quarts cold water, stir in orange juice and garlic. Submerge pork and refrigerate 18–24 hours. Pat dry.

Pulse garlic, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper in food processor to coarse paste. With processor running add orange juice, vinegar, and oil. Rub paste all over pork and into slits. Wrap and rest at room temperature for 1 hour.

Heat oven to 325°F with rack lower-middle. Put pork skin-side down on rack in foil-lined baking sheet; roast 3 hours. Flip skin-side up and roast about 3 hours more, until meat near bone reaches 190°F and is very tender. Tent skin if too dark.
Rest 1 hour. Remove skin, scrape off top fat layer, cut meat off bone in large pieces, and slice ¼ inch thick. Scrape underside of skin and cut into strips. Serve with Mojo Sauce.
notes: Brine 18–24 hours before cooking; serve crispy skin with pork.

title: Mojo Sauce
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
steps: Heat oil in medium saucepan over medium heat until shimmering. Cook garlic, salt, and cumin until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Off heat, whisk in vinegar, orange juice, oregano, and pepper. Cool completely and whisk to recombine before serving.

title: Classic Vanilla Pudding
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
steps: Heat 2½ cups milk, sugar, and salt over medium heat until simmering.
Whisk cornstarch and remaining ¼ cup milk smooth. Whisk in yolks.
Slowly whisk hot milk into yolk mixture to temper.
Return to saucepan and whisk constantly over medium heat until thickened and 175–180°F, about 1 minute. Off heat whisk in butter and vanilla; strain into bowl.
Press lightly oiled parchment flush against pudding surface. Refrigerate until cold and set, at least 3 hours. Whisk smooth before serving.

title: Crème Anglaise
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
steps: Split vanilla bean and scrape seeds. Bring bean, seeds, milk, and salt to simmer. Cover off heat and steep 20 minutes.
Whisk yolks and sugar smooth. Slowly whisk in hot milk to temper. Return to saucepan and stir constantly over low heat until sauce thickens slightly and reaches 175–180°F, 5–7 minutes.
Strain, discard bean, cover and chill about 45 minutes. Refrigerate up to 3 days with wrap touching surface.
Orange variation: Substitute two 3-inch strips orange zest for vanilla bean; add 1 tablespoon Grand Marnier after straining.
Coffee variation: Add 1½ teaspoons instant espresso powder to saucepan with vanilla bean and seeds.
Earl Grey variation: Substitute 1 Earl Grey tea bag for vanilla bean; remove after steeping.
notes: Vanilla extract alternative: use 1 teaspoon instead of bean, skip steeping, and add after straining.

title: Lemon Curd
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: 3 large eggs plus 5 large egg yolks
6 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into ½-inch pieces and frozen
steps: Heat lemon juice, sugar, and salt over medium-high heat until sugar dissolves and mixture is hot but not boiling, about 1 minute.
Whisk eggs and yolks together. Slowly whisk hot lemon mixture into eggs to temper. Return to saucepan and cook over medium-low, stirring constantly, until thickened and 170–175°F.
Off heat stir in frozen butter until melted. Strain into bowl and press plastic wrap against surface. Chill until firm and spreadable, at least 1½ hours. Refrigerate up to 3 days.

title: Best Ground Beef Chili
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: 3 ounces (6–8) dried ancho chiles, stemmed, seeded, torn into ½-inch pieces (1½ cups)
1–2 teaspoons minced canned chipotle chile in adobo sauce
Lime wedges, cilantro, chopped red onion, for serving
steps: Heat oven to 275°F. Toss beef with 2 tablespoons water, salt, and baking soda; rest 20 minutes.

Toast anchos in Dutch oven over medium-high heat, 2–6 minutes; cool 5 minutes. Process with tortilla chips, cumin, coriander, paprika, garlic powder, oregano, peppercorns, and thyme until finely ground, about 3 minutes. Puree tomatoes and juice separately.

Heat oil in Dutch oven. Soften onion about 5 minutes, add garlic for 30 seconds. Add beef and brown 12–14 minutes, breaking into ¼-inch pieces. Stir in spice mixture and chipotle for 1–2 minutes. Add beans with liquid, sugar, tomatoes, and remaining 2 cups water; simmer. Cover and cook in oven 1½–2 hours until tender and slightly thickened.
Rest uncovered 10 minutes, stir vinegar and recombine fat with chili. Salt to taste; serve with lime, cilantro, and red onion.
notes: Photo does not show cookbook page number. More chipotle makes a spicier chili.

title: Apple-Mustard Glazed Pork Loin
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: ⅔ cup apple cider or apple juice
1 (2½–3-pound) boneless pork loin roast, fat trimmed to ¼ inch, tied at 1½-inch intervals
steps: Whisk cider, apple butter, whole-grain mustard, vinegar, dry mustard, and salt in bowl.
Boil water and sugar over medium-high heat without stirring until straw-colored, 3–4 minutes. Reduce heat and swirl until amber, 1–2 minutes (360–370°F).
Off heat carefully whisk in cider mixture. Return to medium heat and whisk until caramel dissolves and sauce thickens, about 2 minutes. Cool to room temperature.
Heat oven to 375°F. Pat roast dry, season with salt and pepper. Brown on all sides in oil in 12-inch ovensafe skillet, about 10 minutes.
Off heat add glaze; turn roast to coat. Roast in skillet until center registers 140°F, 35–45 minutes, turning twice to coat.
Rest roast 15–20 minutes. Let glaze thicken slightly, remove twine, coat roast in skillet, slice ¼ inch thick and serve with glaze.

title: Foolproof Hollandaise Sauce
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: Pinch cayenne pepper, plus extra to season
16 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted and hot (180°F)
steps: Blend yolks, lemon juice, salt, and cayenne until frothy, about 10 seconds, scraping blender as needed.

With blender running, slowly add hot melted butter; blend until emulsified, about 2 minutes. Thin with hot water as needed until sauce drips slowly from spoon. Adjust salt and cayenne; serve immediately.
notes: Variations: Mustard-Dill Hollandaise: blend 1 tablespoon whole-grain mustard and 1 tablespoon minced fresh dill into finished sauce, combined but not smooth. Saffron Hollandaise: add ⅛ teaspoon crumbled saffron threads to blender with yolks.

title: Foolproof Béarnaise Sauce
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: 2 sprigs fresh tarragon, plus 1½ tablespoons minced fresh tarragon, divided
Pinch cayenne pepper, plus extra to season
16 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted and hot (180°F)
steps: Simmer vinegar, shallot, and tarragon sprigs in 8-inch skillet until about 2 tablespoons vinegar remain, 5–7 minutes. Discard shallot and sprigs.

Blend yolks, vinegar reduction, salt, and cayenne until frothy, about 10 seconds. With blender running, slowly add hot butter and blend until emulsified, about 2 minutes. Add minced tarragon and pulse about 10 times, combined but not smooth. Thin with hot water as needed; season and serve immediately.

title: Mayonnaise
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: 1 tablespoon water, plus extra as needed
steps: Blend egg yolks, lemon juice, water, mustard, sugar, and salt about 10 seconds. With blender running, slowly add oil and process until emulsified, about 2 minutes.
Thin with extra water if needed. Season with salt and pepper to taste; refrigerate up to 3 days.
notes: Variations: Aioli: add 2 peeled and smashed garlic cloves to blender with egg yolks. Smoked Paprika Mayonnaise: substitute lime juice for lemon juice; add 1½ teaspoons smoked paprika, ¼ teaspoon ground cumin, and 1 small peeled smashed garlic clove with yolks. Contains raw egg yolks.

title: Classic Pot Roast
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: 1 (3½–4-pound) boneless beef chuck-eye roast, pulled apart at seams and trimmed
¾ cup dry red wine, divided
1 sprig fresh thyme plus ¼ teaspoon chopped
steps: Salt meat pieces and let stand on wire rack at room temperature 1 hour.

Heat oven to 300°F. Melt butter in Dutch oven over medium heat. Soften onions 8–10 minutes. Add carrot and celery for 5 minutes; garlic for 30 seconds. Stir in 1 cup broth, ½ cup wine, tomato paste, bay leaf, and thyme sprig; simmer.
Pat meat dry, season with pepper, and tie three pieces into two evenly shaped roasts with kitchen twine.
Nestle meat on vegetables. Cover pot tightly with foil and lid; roast 3½–4 hours until fork-tender, turning meat halfway. Transfer meat to bowl, tent with foil.

Strain cooking liquid into measuring cup. Discard bay leaf and thyme; rest 5 minutes and skim fat. Add remaining broth to reach 3 cups liquid. Blend vegetables with liquid until smooth, about 2 minutes. Simmer sauce in saucepan.
Remove twine and slice meat against grain ½ inch thick. Add remaining ¼ cup wine, chopped thyme, and balsamic vinegar to sauce; season. Spoon half over meat and pass remaining sauce.

source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
steps: Whisk all ingredients together in a bowl.
notes: For a spicier sauce, add hot sauce to taste.
title: Lexington Vinegar Barbecue Sauce

source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
steps: Whisk all ingredients together in a bowl.
notes: Use light or dark brown sugar.
title: South Carolina Mustard Barbecue Sauce

source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
steps: Whisk all ingredients together in a bowl.
notes: Mild molasses is preferred.
title: Sweet and Tangy Barbecue Sauce

source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
steps: Adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 450°F. Toast cornmeal in 10-inch cast-iron skillet over medium heat, stirring frequently, until fragrant, about 3 minutes. Transfer cornmeal to large bowl, whisk in sour cream and milk, and set aside.

Wipe skillet clean. Add oil to skillet, place in oven, and heat until oil shimmers, about 10 minutes. Carefully remove skillet and add butter, swirling to incorporate. Pour all but 1 tablespoon of the oil-butter mixture into cornmeal mixture and whisk. Add sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt; whisk to combine. Whisk in eggs.

Quickly scrape batter into skillet with remaining fat and smooth top. Bake until top begins to crack and sides are golden brown, 12–15 minutes, rotating skillet halfway. Cool on wire rack at least 15 minutes before serving.
notes: Variation — Southern-Style Jalapeño-Lime Cornbread: Whisk 2 minced jalapeño chiles and 2 teaspoons grated lime zest into cornmeal mixture with eggs. Use fine- or medium-ground cornmeal, not coarse-ground.
title: Southern-Style Cornbread

source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: 1¼ cups warm tap water, plus extra as needed
steps: Mix masa harina, oil, and salt in medium bowl, then fold in water with rubber spatula. Knead by hand in bowl, adding extra water 1 tablespoon at a time until dough is soft and tacky but not sticky, like Play-Doh. Cover with damp dish towel and rest 5 minutes.

Cut sides of 1-quart zipper-lock bag, leaving bottom seam intact. Line large plate with 2 damp dish towels. Divide dough into 12 equal portions (about 2 tablespoons each), roll into smooth balls, and keep between towels. Place one ball between sides of zipper-lock bag and press into a 6-inch circle using pie plate. Keep in plastic until skillet is hot.

Heat 10-inch cast-iron skillet over medium heat for 5 minutes. Peel off top plastic, flip tortilla into palm, peel off remaining plastic, and lay in skillet. Cook without moving until tortilla moves freely when skillet is shaken and shrinks slightly, about 45 seconds.

Flip and cook until edges curl and bottom is spotty brown, about 1 minute. Flip back and cook until first side is spotty brown and puffs slightly in center, 30–60 seconds. Keep cooked tortilla between damp dish towels and repeat. Serve.
notes: Cooled tortillas can be layered between parchment, wrapped in plastic wrap, and refrigerated for up to 5 days.
title: Homemade Corn Tortillas
Homemade Taco-Size Flour Tortillas
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: 5 tablespoons vegetable shortening, cut into ½-inch chunks
steps: Combine flour and salt in large bowl. Rub shortening into flour with fingers until mixture resembles coarse meal. Fold in warm water with rubber spatula.
Knead briefly on counter into smooth ball. Divide into 12 portions, roll into balls, cover and refrigerate until firm, at least 30 minutes or up to 2 days.
Cut twelve 6-inch parchment squares. Roll each ball into a 6-inch circle on lightly floured counter, stacking with parchment between.

Heat oil in 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat until shimmering; wipe with paper towel to leave a thin film. Cook each tortilla until surface bubbles and underside is spotty brown, about 1 minute; adjust heat if browning too quickly. Flip and cook second side until spotty brown, 30–45 seconds. Cover finished tortillas with clean dish towel and repeat.
notes: Cooled tortillas may be layered between parchment, wrapped in plastic, and refrigerated for up to 3 days.

title: No-Churn Vanilla Ice Cream
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
steps: Blend chilled cream until soft peaks form, 20–30 seconds. Scrape sides and continue until stiff peaks form, about 10 seconds. Stir in condensed milk, whole milk, corn syrup, sugar, vanilla, and salt. Blend until combined, about 20 seconds.
Pour into 8½-by-4½-inch loaf pan, press plastic wrap against surface, and freeze until firm, at least 6 hours.
notes: Variations (modify base): Birthday Cake—vanilla 2 tsp; add ½ cup vanilla frosting and ⅛ tsp yellow coloring with condensed milk, fold in 2 tbsp rainbow sprinkles before freezing. Salted Caramel–Coconut—vanilla 1 tsp, salt ½ tsp, caramel sauce instead of corn syrup; fold in ¼ cup toasted sweetened coconut, swirl ⅓ cup caramel sauce. Mint-Cookie—replace vanilla with ¾ tsp peppermint extract; add ⅛ tsp green coloring; fold in ½ cup crushed Oreos. Peach Cobbler—omit sugar, use bourbon instead of vanilla; add ½ cup peach preserves and ¼ tsp cinnamon with condensed milk; fold in ½ cup chopped shortbread cookies. Key Lime—omit vanilla; use buttermilk instead of whole milk; add ½ cup limeade concentrate with condensed milk; fold in ½ cup crushed graham crackers. Strawberry-Buttermilk—use ½ cup buttermilk instead of whole milk and 1 tsp lemon juice instead of vanilla; swirl ⅓ cup strawberry jam. Banana–Walnut–Chocolate Chunk—omit vanilla; add 2 ripe bananas with condensed milk; fold in ¼ cup toasted walnuts and ¼ cup bittersweet chocolate. Peanut Butter Cup—omit vanilla; add ½ cup creamy peanut butter with condensed milk; fold in ½ cup chopped peanut butter cups. Dark Chocolate—vanilla 1 tsp; add 6 oz melted bittersweet chocolate and ½ tsp instant espresso powder with condensed milk. Milk Chocolate—vanilla 1 tsp; add 6 oz melted milk chocolate with condensed milk. Malted Milk Chocolate—vanilla 1 tsp; add 6 oz melted milk chocolate and 6 tbsp malted milk powder with condensed milk.

title: Flaky Buttermilk Biscuits
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: 16 tablespoons (2 sticks) unsalted butter, frozen for 30 minutes
steps: Line rimmed baking sheet with parchment. Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt. Coat frozen butter sticks in flour and grate 7 tablespoons from each into flour. Toss; reserve remaining 2 tablespoons butter.
Fold buttermilk into flour just until combined. Turn onto generously floured counter and press into rough 7-inch square.

Roll to 12-by-9-inch rectangle, fold into thirds, turn 90 degrees. Repeat rolling/folding/turning four more times (five folds total). Roll into 8½-inch square about 1 inch thick; cover and refrigerate 30 minutes. Heat oven to 400°F.
Trim ¼ inch off each side, cut into 9 squares, space at least 1 inch apart. Melt reserved butter and brush tops.
Bake 22–25 minutes until golden, rotating sheet halfway. Cool on wire rack 15 minutes.
notes: Use cold ingredients; dough may look dry initially. Do not add extra buttermilk.

title: Grill-Smoked Chicken with Fragrant Spice Rub
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: ½ cup table salt for brining
steps: Dissolve salt in 2 quarts cold water. Brine chicken 1 hour refrigerated (skip brine for kosher chicken). Pat dry; loosen breast/thigh skin, rub spice mixture over skin and underneath; tuck wingtips.
Soak wood chips 15 minutes, drain, and wrap into two foil packets with 1 cup chips each. Cut two 2-inch slits in each packet.

Open bottom kettle grill vent halfway; place disposable pan in center. Light chimney starter filled with 6 quarts charcoal. Divide lit coals into two piles on either side of pan; put one wood packet on each pile. Install grate, cover, open lid vent halfway and heat until smoking, about 5 minutes.
Clean and oil grate. Place chicken breast side down above pan; cover with lid vent over chicken and cook 30 minutes.
Turn chicken breast side up, cover and cook until breast reaches 160°F and thighs 175°F, 25–35 minutes. Rest 20 minutes before carving.
notes: Uses separate Fragrant Spice Rub recipe R137.

title: Fragrant Spice Rub

steps: Mix all spices in a small bowl. Store leftover spice rub for up to 3 months.
notes: Companion to Grill-Smoked Chicken (R136).

title: Gravlax
source: 100 Techniques: Essentials Every Home Cook Should Know
ingredients: ⅓ cup packed light brown sugar
steps: Mix brown sugar and salt. Place salmon skin side down in 13-by-9-inch glass baking dish; drizzle with brandy, coat with sugar-salt mixture, and press dill on top.
Cover loosely with plastic wrap, top with another baking dish or pie plate, and weigh down with heavy cans. Refrigerate about 3 days until firm, basting once daily with released liquid.
Scrape dill away, remove salmon and pat dry before thinly slicing. Refrigerate unsliced gravlax tightly wrapped up to 1 week; slice just before serving.
notes: For easier slicing, freeze for 30 minutes before slicing. Raw cured fish is not cooked; use fish suitable for raw consumption and keep refrigerated.
